held_from.description: When the reader's share is held — its Holding time, four days before the cut-off — while it is only checked and that is ahead at `read_at` (`share_state` `CHECKED`, #639). `null` on every other line.

taken_at.title: Taken At
taken_at.description: When the shares are taken — the club's cut-off — or were: the cut-off, or when a game booked after it was booked. Present exactly when `share_state` is.

free_to_leave_until.title: Free To Leave Until
free_to_leave_until.description: The club's cut-off while it is still ahead at `read_at`: leaving before it takes nothing — the hold on the card is let go — so the line says *free to leave until Fri 17:00* (Q113). `null` from the cut-off on, for a game that filled after it, for a game still waiting for its club, and for a reader not on the game. The line switches by itself at this instant.

refunded_grosze.title: Refunded Grosze
refunded_grosze.description: What everybody still in is given back — the whole share, on a game its club cancelled after the cut-off had taken it (*refunded 30 zł*). `null` where nothing is: a game short at its cut-off, or cancelled before it, took nothing (#637).

BookedMoneySchema.title: BookedMoneySchema
BookedMoneySchema.description:
The money line: *30 zł · free to leave until Fri 17:00* while the share
is held, *Paid · 30 zł* once it is taken (#637; the mechanics §14.1,
Q113).

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: The booking — the same id the game had while it filled.

BookedSchema.title: BookedSchema
BookedSchema.description: The game a yes booked — *It's a game!*

BookedSidesSchema.title: BookedSidesSchema
BookedSidesSchema.description:
The sides the game was booked with, **the reader's first, with them first
on it** — *You + Piotr vs Inés + Bartek*.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole — the tile may cut it short, never invent a first name. `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived link to their first photograph; `null` with `photo_id` draws a poster.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the game's sport; `null` if unrated.

paid.title: Paid
paid.description: Their share was taken — the *paid* tag. `false` while the game waits for a payment, on a game that was never booked, and on the reader's own tile when they are not on the game but offered its open seat — the dashed *You?* (#545).

BookedTileSchema.title: BookedTileSchema
BookedTileSchema.description: One seat on a booked game.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The ordinary Game it opened: its result acts, its balance forecast (`GET /games/{id}/pairing`) and its room in `GET /conversations` are all reached by this id. `null` on a game that waited for a payment and was never booked.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant the status and money line were folded against.

status.description: `BOOKED` — full and booked, its hour still ahead. `NEEDS_RESULT` — its hour has come and nobody has said it happened. `CONFIRM_THE_RESULT` — a score is on the table. `COUNTED` — a score is agreed. `UNCOUNTED` — they played and no score is agreed: two scores named different winners (no `uncounted_reason`), or one of the reasons `uncounted_reason` names. `PLAYED_NO_SCORE` — full at its hour, and nobody recorded it before the entry window closed: played for everybody on it, and no Level moves. `CALLED_OFF` — it will not be played; `called_off_reason` says why. `SEAT_OPEN` — somebody left and the seat is offered (`open_seats`); before the cut-off (`money.free_to_leave_until`) *fills by then or the game is off and everyone is refunded*, after it *the game goes ahead*. A game whose hour comes with a seat still open is `UNCOUNTED` with `uncounted_reason` `SEAT_EMPTY`. **`WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT`** (#625; Q111) — full, and one player's share was refused when it filled: *Waiting for one payment · until `payment_due_by` · Nobody pays until it's in*. Nobody paid, there is no Game and no court given, and it asks nothing of the reader (`needs_you` is `false`); to the payer it reads *Confirm your payment by `your_payment_due_by`* — *Fix your card by …* before the cut-off (`time_to`, #638) — beside their *To confirm* row. Paid in time it is `BOOKED`; out of time it is `SEAT_OPEN` with `filling_again` — and so is a game one of the others left meanwhile. **`SEAT_OPEN` with `filling_again`** (Q106) — a full game that went back to filling before it was booked: a payment it waited for did not come in time, or a seat opened while it waited — a player left, their week filled, or two players stopped fitting. Nobody paid, there is no Game and no court, and it asks nothing of the reader (`needs_you` is `false`): *1 seat open · books when it's full · nobody paid*. It is in the reader's live yeses too, where *Withdraw* (`DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes`, the same id) takes it off their Home. Full again, it reads `BOOKED`; `CALLED_OFF` if its book-by passes first. No club confirms a game: nothing on Home waits for a club's answer (#669).

called_off_reason.description: Why a `CALLED_OFF` game will not be played — `null` on every other status. `BOOK_BY_PASSED` — a game that went back to filling reached its book-by before it was full again: nobody paid. `COURT_HOUR_LOST` — a game that went back to filling lost its court to another game before it was full again — or before the payment it waited for came in: nobody paid, and its players are dealt a new card first. `PAYMENT_NOT_IN_TIME` — a payment the game waited for did not come in time and it could no longer fill: the book-by had come (#625). Nobody paid. `SHORT_AT_THE_CUT_OFF` — a seat that opened before the club's cut-off was still empty at it: everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`); read off the clock from the cut-off on. `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` — the club cancelled it, with its reason (`club_cancel_reason`): everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`), it is on nobody's record, and they are dealt a new card first (#547).

club_cancel_reason.description: Why the club cancelled a `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` game — `WEATHER`, `REPAIR`, `DOUBLE_BOOKING` or `OTHER` (no reason given). `null` on every other game.

uncounted_reason.description: Why an `UNCOUNTED` game is uncounted with nobody disagreeing about a score — `null` otherwise. `SEAT_EMPTY` — its hour came with a seat open: somebody left after the cut-off and nobody took the seat. No Level moved, and nothing is on the record of those who stayed. `DIDNT_COME` — somebody was tapped *isn't here yet* at the court and never arrived (#657; `GET /games` — `attendance`): the game takes no score and never counts. For a day it is provisional — their *I was there*, confirmed by somebody else on the court, makes them Came late and the game carries on.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats a leaver left open — the dashed tiles; nought unless `SEAT_OPEN`. The sides list the seats still held. On a game `filling_again`, the seats nobody is In on, the sides listing everybody In now.

filling_again.title: Filling Again
filling_again.description: A full game that went back to filling before it was booked (#625, Q106) — `SEAT_OPEN` while it fills, nobody paid; `CALLED_OFF` once its book-by passes, or its court goes, before it is full again. `false` on every booked game.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: The court the game was given — *Court 2*. `null` on a game that was never booked, which no court was given.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: The court's kind — *Court 2 · indoor* — which follows a move (Q122). `null` with `court_name`.

payment_due_by.title: Payment Due By
payment_due_by.description: When the payment the game waits for is due — *Waiting for one payment · until 14:40 · Nobody pays until it's in* (#625; Q111): a share was refused, and its player's seat is theirs alone until then. Never names whose payment it is. `null` unless `WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT`. Like `free_to_leave_until`, the line switches by itself at this instant.

your_payment_due_by.title: Your Payment Due By
your_payment_due_by.description: **The reader's own** refused share and their time to pay — *Confirm your payment by 14:40*, or before the cut-off *Fix your card by 14:40* (`time_to`, #638) — while it runs, on a game waiting for it or one gone back to filling meanwhile (#625). The payment is their *To confirm* row's (`GET /players/me/payments-to-confirm`). **A rescuer whose share was refused** reads, from outside, the seat kept for them alone until then (#640) — *Fix your card by 14:40 to take the seat*, or after the cut-off *Confirm your payment by 14:40* — offered to nobody else meanwhile. `null` for everybody else, and from the moment it runs out.

time_to.description: What the time to `payment_due_by` and `your_payment_due_by` is for (#638; Q113). `FIX_THE_CARD` — the hold was refused **before the club's cut-off**, where nothing is taken, only held: the payer reads *Fix your card by 14:40 to keep your seat* — nothing is paid now — and the time never runs past the cut-off. `PAY` — refused from the cut-off on, where the money is taken at once: *Confirm your payment by 14:40*. The others read *Waiting for one payment* either way. `null` while neither is set.

shows_forecast.title: Shows Forecast
shows_forecast.description: Draw the balance forecast — `GET /games/{game_id}/pairing`, the card today's game screen draws — while the full game awaits its entry. `false` while a seat is open and once a result is told.

leaving.description: What *Leave the game* would cost now — the line under the button and its sheet (`POST /bookings/{id}/departure`). `null` where there is no button: once the hour has come, on a game that is over, for a reader not on the game, and on a game `filling_again`, whose way out is a game still filling's — *Withdraw*, `DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes`.

rescue.description: Present for a reader **not on the game** whom its open seat is offered to — a Seat open card, a Seats to fill row (#545): they stand in the seat that opened first, unpaid (*You?*), and **I'm in · `money.share_grosze`** is `POST /bookings/{id}/seats`. No Chat and no Leave. `null` for a player in it.

BookingDetailsResponse.title: BookingDetailsResponse
BookingDetailsResponse.description:
A booked game's details, for a player in it — or for a member its open
seat is offered to (#545).

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). ``null`` where ``users`` no longer has the account — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step.

CalledOffBySchema.title: CalledOffBySchema
CalledOffBySchema.description:
Who called the game off, and what they are called (``docs/adr/0172`` §4).

**The name is carried because the court cannot supply it**: the leaver whose
departure called the game off has been **vacated** — their seat is drawn
`player_id: null` — so the seats alone could not name them. It is the same
name a seat carries, read in the same set read, and it is `null` for the
same reason a seat's is: an account `users` no longer answers for.

**A departure is told from a press by whether this player still holds a
seat on the game.** The presser does; the leaver's seat is open. No second
field says which — the record already does.

CalledOffReason.title: CalledOffReason
CalledOffReason.description: Why a game will not be played (the mechanics §14.1).

starts_on.title: Starts On
starts_on.description: Its Monday, on the club's clock.

CappedWeekSchema.title: CappedWeekSchema
CappedWeekSchema.description:
A week the player has as many games booked in as they allow: nothing is
dealt for it.

CardType.title: CardType
CardType.description: The three cards a deck deals (the mechanics §8.1).

gender_preference.description:
Who this player is willing to be matched with.

**It is mutual and durable.** Narrowing it makes them invisible to the excluded side entirely — including to searchers who asked for anybody — and the client must say so at the moment of setting; learning it from silence is not acceptable. Seats already accepted are facts, not candidates: nothing already agreed is undone.

ChangeGenderPreferenceRequest.title: ChangeGenderPreferenceRequest
ChangeGenderPreferenceRequest.description: A new durable answer to *who am I willing to play with*.

gender.description: The player's own answer. `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` is a first-class answer; it matches only unconstrained preferences, which costs its holder reach, and the client is what says so at the moment of asking (`docs/adr/0096`).

ChangeGenderRequest.title: ChangeGenderRequest
ChangeGenderRequest.description: A new answer to the gender question — *self-declared, freely changed*.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description: The new line, or `null` to withdraw it. Trimmed, then held to **at most 100 characters** and **one line** — the commit's fence exactly, with the commit's codes: `intro_not_admitted` and one coarse `details.reason`, `too_long`, `multiline`, or `contains_contact` for a phone number, an email, a URL or bare domain, or an `@handle`. Whitespace is `null`: a line with nothing in it is withdrawn, never stored empty.

ChangeIntroRequest.title: ChangeIntroRequest
ChangeIntroRequest.description:
The line, replaced — or withdrawn (``docs/adr/0179`` §6).

**The field is required and nullable**, which is the shape of a value whose
absence is a real act: ``null`` withdraws the line, and ``{}`` is a 422 so
that a client which forgot the field cannot be clearing lines. No
``max_length``, for the commit's reason: the cap is the domain's, and the
domain refuses with `intro_not_admitted` and `reason: too_long`, which is
the code a client branches on.

**Nothing comes back.** The intro reaches the card, the record and its
author's own profile read and nowhere else — a sweep in ``tests/unit/
test_intro.py`` holds the contract to those three shapes — and a response
that echoed the trimmed line would be a fourth. The author reads it back
from the profile read, as the two gender writes are read back.

ChangeLocationRequest.title: ChangeLocationRequest
ChangeLocationRequest.description:
The phone's fix, on a cold start.

**What is sent is never what is kept.** The client sends the fix its device
gave it, with the accuracy onboarding used; the platform rounds it to the
cell about a kilometre across before anything is recorded, exactly as the
commit does, and a fix that rounds to the cell already stored records
nothing (``docs/adr/0174`` §6). Nothing comes back: no route on this
surface serves the area yet — the profile read grows the field when *You*
is built — and a silent write on every launch is not the one to start.

The bounds are the world's, as they are on the commit's ``location`` —
read from the value object rather than spelled again. A fix outside them
is a broken reading and not a place, refused at the boundary rather than
rounded into a cell at the pole.

photo_ids.title: Photo Ids
photo_ids.description: Ids returned by `POST /photos`, in the order the player arranged them — the first is the one a player card shows. At most 3; **an empty list is valid and clears**. Every id is checked to exist and to belong to this player, exactly as the commit checks it, and the same id twice is refused with `duplicate_photo`.

ChangePhotosRequest.title: ChangePhotosRequest
ChangePhotosRequest.description:
The photographs, replaced whole and **in order** (``docs/adr/0179`` §8).

An empty list is a legal value and clears: a profile may hold none, and the
poster returns. There is no *clear my photos* flag for the week's reason —
the list is the answer.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: Every tag this player now holds, as ids served by `GET /player-profile/options`. **The list is the selection** — what is absent is dropped. Re-checked against the served vocabulary and the served floor and ceiling exactly as the commit re-checks them; the same id twice is refused with `duplicate_social_tag`.

ChangeSocialTagsRequest.title: ChangeSocialTagsRequest
ChangeSocialTagsRequest.description:
The Social tags, replaced whole (``docs/adr/0179`` §8).

Strings rather than an enum, as the commit carries them: an id outside the
served vocabulary is refused by the domain with ``unknown_social_tag``, a
count outside the served bounds with ``social_tag_selection_out_of_bounds``,
and the client gets a code it can act on rather than a 422.

ClaimCodeRequest.title: ClaimCodeRequest
ClaimCodeRequest.description:
The address and the 8-character code from the email. The code is read
forgivingly — case, spaces and dashes are ignored — and its length is not
checked here: a code of the wrong length is simply not the right code, and
is told ``code_incorrect`` as every other one is. The bound is a cap on
what a request may carry, not a rule about codes.

ClaimInvitationRequest.title: ClaimInvitationRequest
ClaimInvitationRequest.description:
*Have an invitation code?*: the address and the 8-character code. The
code is read forgivingly — case, spaces and dashes are ignored — and its
length is not checked here: a code of the wrong length is simply not the
right code.

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.description: Present it as `ticket` when setting the new password. Good for `expires_in` seconds, and never past the code's own hour; claiming the code again replaces it.

ClaimTicketResponse.title: ClaimTicketResponse
ClaimTicketResponse.description: A correct code, exchanged for a ticket the new password is set with.

ClubCancelReason.title: ClubCancelReason
ClubCancelReason.description:
Why the club cancelled a booked game (the mechanics §16.9) — the players
are told it with their refund.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: From the reader's Location area to the club, one decimal and never below `0.1`. **`null` for a reader with no Location area**, whose clubs come A–Z.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the club offers, in the registry's order.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: The biggest crowd first. **Home-club search**: every group at the club — and a club with some is the one the New group form tints and tags *group already here*. **Join search**: every group when the club itself matched, only the groups whose name matched when it did not, and exactly the linked group for a link. Empty for a club with none: *no groups here yet*.

ClubCardSchema.title: ClubCardSchema
ClubCardSchema.description:
One club as a search draws it: its header — which is context, not a
choice — and the groups inside it.

ClubNameSchema.title: ClubNameSchema
ClubNameSchema.description: The group's home club, as a line under its name.

social_tag_ids.title: Social Tag Ids
social_tag_ids.description: The tag ids this player picked, as served by `GET /player-profile/options`. The count is re-checked against the served floor and ceiling, and an id this platform does not serve is refused with `unknown_social_tag`.

photo_ids.title: Photo Ids
photo_ids.description: Ids returned by `POST /photos`, in the order the player arranged them — the first is the one a player card shows. At most 3; an empty list is valid. Every id is checked to exist and to belong to this player.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly Hours
weekly_hours.description: The hours of the week this player ticked. **At least one of the 112** — an empty list is refused with `weekly_hours_empty`. The minimum is exactly one and is not served: it is fixed, so a client holds it as a constant. Repeated hours are collapsed, and the floor is counted after that.

gender.description: The player's own answer, asked once. Required — `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` is a first-class answer and is what a player who does not want to say sends; there is no way to send nothing. It matches only unconstrained preferences, which costs its holder reach, and the client is what says so at the moment of asking.

gender_preference.description:
Who this player is willing to be matched with. Optional, and `ANY` when it is not sent.

**It is mutual and durable.** It governs what reaches this player as well as what this player sees, so narrowing it makes them invisible to the excluded side entirely — including to searchers who asked for anybody. The client must say so at the moment of setting; learning it from silence is not acceptable. A single search may narrow this further and nothing may widen past it.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description:
One line about yourself — your **intro** — or nothing. Optional: a player who skips the step sends nothing (or `null`, or whitespace, which is the same), and has no intro rather than an empty one.

Trimmed, then held to **at most 100 characters** and **one line**, in any language. Refused with `intro_not_admitted` and one coarse `details.reason` — `too_long`, `multiline`, or `contains_contact` for a phone number, an email, a URL or bare domain, or an `@handle` — so the client can say what to change without the server explaining what it matched. Nothing else is read.

Edited later from the You tab through `PUT /players/me/intro`, with the tags and the photos it sits between (ADR-0179 §6). It crosses on the player card and on the record, and this response does not echo it.

CommitPlayerProfileRequest.title: CommitPlayerProfileRequest
CommitPlayerProfileRequest.description:
Every answer from onboarding's second part, in one body.

**Photos and the intro are the fields with a default**, because holding no
photograph is a legitimate answer to *add some photos* and writing nothing
is a legitimate answer to *say it in your own words* (``docs/adr/0170``).
Everything else is something this request must actually carry — a
location, a tag selection, a gender answer, and **a week with something
ticked in it** (``docs/adr/0102``).

The week's *floor* is not spelled here, and that is the same decision the tag
selection's is: an empty list passes this schema and is refused by the domain
with ``weekly_hours_empty``, so the client gets a code it can branch on
and a recovery it can offer, rather than a 422 that can only say some field
somewhere was wrong.

ConfidenceReasonResponse.title: ConfidenceReasonResponse
ConfidenceReasonResponse.description: Why confidence landed where it did: a stable key and the sentence shown.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant this list was folded. It earns one because **its very membership is a fold**: a room is destroyed rather than delisted, so whether a row appears at all was decided against this instant.

ConversationListResponse.title: ConversationListResponse
ConversationListResponse.description: Every room you are a member of, the ones that moved last first.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who they are, and what a line's `actor_id` and a message's `author_id` match

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **`null` for an account `users` can no longer name** — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The person keeps their place either way: a member dropped would draw a three-person doubles court, and an actor dropped would leave a line naming nobody. Draw the unknown player's mark for `null` and nothing else. Nothing may derive a familiar form from it, and it is never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere (``docs/adr/0171``).

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — the two travel as a pair or not at all.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**. It expires within minutes and is not a stored value.

ConversationMemberSchema.title: ConversationMemberSchema
ConversationMemberSchema.description:
One person on the game's court right now.

**Derived from the game's line-up, never stored** (``docs/adr/0146`` §7), and
it **moves with the court**: somebody who left is not drawn, and a rescue who
took the seat is, the moment either commits.

**The same four fields as a person, and a narrower claim.** Being on the
list is the fact; the face is `ConversationPersonSchema`'s. A member is
always among the response's `people` too, resolved in the same read, so the
two lists cannot disagree about a current member.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who they are, and what a line's `actor_id` and a message's `author_id` match

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **`null` for an account `users` can no longer name** — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The person keeps their place either way: a member dropped would draw a three-person doubles court, and an actor dropped would leave a line naming nobody. Draw the unknown player's mark for `null` and nothing else. Nothing may derive a familiar form from it, and it is never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere (``docs/adr/0171``).

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — the two travel as a pair or not at all.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**. It expires within minutes and is not a stored value.

ConversationPersonSchema.title: ConversationPersonSchema
ConversationPersonSchema.description:
One person this response names — **a name and a face, and nothing else.**

No Level, no band, no area, no score — those are a *card*'s, and a card is
what somebody reads to decide about a game that might happen. Everybody
here was on this court or spoke in this room.

**The shape `people` is a list of, and the shape a member has.** A member is
a person who is on the court *right now*; somebody who spoke here and left
the court since is not, and is still somebody the page has to name. One
shape for both, so a client resolves every `actor_id` and `author_id` the
same way.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant the header and the page were folded — **one instant for both**, so members and entries can never disagree.

people.title: People
people.description: Everybody this response names, resolved once against `read_at` and ordered by id: the members, and every author and actor in `entries`. **A superset of `members`**, so a current member is the same face in both. Fill every `{name}` and every author label from here, and merge each page's `people` into it as you page back.

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: The newest page, **oldest first inside it**. Page backward from `entries[0].seq` through `GET /conversations/{id}/entries`; you have the beginning when you hold `seq` 1.

ConversationResponse.title: ConversationResponse
ConversationResponse.description: One room's header **and** its newest page, from one fold.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: The booking whose game opened it. **A room is opened only by a booked game**, so this is the booking every room is found by.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The booked game this room is about. A booked game's room is born about it; `null` only on a room nothing opens any more, which is never served. The join a game's details make to find its chat is `booking_id`.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who is on the game's court right now

people.title: People
people.description: Everybody this row names, resolved once and ordered by id: the members, and whoever `last_entry` is about. **A superset of `members`** — fill `{name}` and the author label from here.

last_entry.title: Last Entry
last_entry.description:
The newest thing in the room, rendered by the same two components the stream uses — never a preview string.

**`null` in a room where nothing has happened yet**, which is a real state rather than an edge case: the opening writes no line, so a room whose game was just booked has no entry at all.

ConversationRowSchema.title: ConversationRowSchema
ConversationRowSchema.description:
One room, as a row in the reader's rooms.

**No state pill, and no standing anywhere on it** (``docs/adr/0148`` §6).
Reading one would make the conversation ask `games` what it is, which it
never does — and it does not need to, because **the last entry is what a
pill would have said.**

CourtState.title: CourtState
CourtState.description: What a yes on the card does (the screens A2.3).

name.title: Name
name.description: *Same name as the WhatsApp group*: trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` or `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE`. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once.**

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group has — **required**, a whole number from 2 to 1024. It limits nothing: more players than this is allowed and honest. Refused with `whatsapp_size_invalid`, `details.field` `whatsapp_size`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the group plays — **required**, and **only the club's**. Ticking one twice is ticking it. Refused with `group_sports_required` for none, or `sport_not_offered_by_club` with the sport in `details.sport` — `details.field` `sports` either way.

CreateOfficialGroupRequest.title: CreateOfficialGroupRequest
CreateOfficialGroupRequest.description:
*New official group*. **The home club is not asked**: it is the club in
the path, fixed.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Never unique. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

home_club_id.title: Home Club Id
home_club_id.description: A club from home-club search — **required**. A club Raketa does not have is `home_club_unknown`, `details.field` `home_club_id`.

CreatePlayerGroupRequest.title: CreatePlayerGroupRequest
CreatePlayerGroupRequest.description:
A player creates a group. **No sport is asked for**: the group plays
whatever its members are rated in (``docs/adr/0183`` §6).

DayRange.title: DayRange
DayRange.description: A third of a day, as a card and the posting grid group hours.

proposal_id.title: Proposal Id
proposal_id.description: The game. On a `SEAT_OPEN` card it is the **booking's** id — the same id the game had while it filled: `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` takes the seat, `POST /bookings/{id}/no` is *not this time*, and `GET /bookings/{id}` its details.

type.description: `PICKED_FOR_YOU`, `CHALLENGE` (a member's post) or `SEAT_OPEN` (a rescue: a booked game that lost a player, dealt to its best fits — #545).

challenger.description: The poster of a challenge; `null` on a pick, and on a challenge once its poster withdrew — *the group challenged you*.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What this player pays if it fills — at once, on a `SEAT_OPEN` card.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the card leaves unfilled — its book-by; on a `SEAT_OPEN` card the club's cut-off, then the start. The client counts down only under 24 h.

in_count.title: In Count
in_count.description: People In on the whole game, every version counted — nought on a `SEAT_OPEN` card, whose players have paid (`paid` on their tiles).

version_count.title: Version Count
version_count.description: Versions the game was dealt in; above one, the card says how many people are In on the whole game.

court.description: `COURT_AVAILABLE` — a yes is a free vote; `BOOK_IT_NOW` — a yes fills the game and books it; `BOOKED` — a rescue: the court is booked, and a yes takes the seat and pays at once.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court — *Court 6* — on a `SEAT_OPEN` card; `null` on a game still filling, which is given one at booking.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: The kind of court the card promises — `true` *Indoor*, `false` *Outdoor* — when every free court it could be booked on is of that kind; `null` when they are mixed, which promises neither (Q122). Shown, never chosen by. On a `SEAT_OPEN` card: the booked court's kind.

no_free_cancellation.title: No Free Cancellation
no_free_cancellation.description: The club's cut-off has already passed for this game.

forecast.description: `null` where it cannot be read: somebody on the card holds no rating in the sport, or nobody faces the reader yet.

DeckCardSchema.title: DeckCardSchema
DeckCardSchema.description: One card, as the reader is dealt it: **their own version** of the game.

DeckChallengerSchema.title: DeckChallengerSchema
DeckChallengerSchema.description: Who a challenge names — *Kuba challenged you*.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

provisional.title: Provisional
provisional.description: A seat is empty and was read as matching its partner.

DeckForecastSchema.title: DeckForecastSchema
DeckForecastSchema.description: How even the game on **this** card is forecast to be, with these sides.

grade.description: *High / Good / Slim overlap*: the hours everybody on the card shares, over the week of whoever has least to give.

cells.title: Cells
cells.description: Twenty-one: day by day from Monday, morning first.

count.title: Count
count.description: Cards of this kind the reader is dealt here.

DeckSegmentSchema.title: DeckSegmentSchema
DeckSegmentSchema.description: One side of the *Competitive · N / For fun · N* switch.

DeckSidesSchema.title: DeckSidesSchema
DeckSidesSchema.description:
The rows are the sides (Q70): the reader's, and the other. A side may be
short of a seat, which the client draws empty.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole — the tile may cut it short, never invent a first name. `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived link to their first photograph; `null` with `photo_id` draws a poster.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the card's sport; `null` if unrated.

is_in.title: Is In
is_in.description: They said yes: the **IN** tag. Nobody else carries a tag — a player still deciding is a plain tile.

paid.title: Paid
paid.description: On a `SEAT_OPEN` card, a player on the booked game — *2,75 · paid* (#545). `false` on a game still filling, and on the reader's own tile, which is the open seat.

intent.description: The declaration. `NO_PREFERENCE` is an **explicit answer** and not an absence — the matcher must be able to tell *either suits me* from *I never opened that screen*, and nobody is ever backfilled to it. There is no null.

surface.description: Which screen this was declared on. Required, because the client is the only party that knows — and safe to take its word for, because nothing branches on it: it is context recorded beside the fact, never a thing a decision reads.

DeclarePlayIntentRequest.title: DeclarePlayIntentRequest
DeclarePlayIntentRequest.description:
What kind of game this player wants in one sport, and where they said so.

The sport is the path, because it is half the resource's identity: the
resource is *one player's intent in one sport* (``docs/adr/0094``).

left.description: `BEFORE_THE_CUT_OFF` — nothing was taken: the hold on the card is let go, nobody is refunded (#637); the seat is offered to others. `AFTER_THE_CUT_OFF` — the seat stays paid and is offered to others until the start; refunded, less exactly the fee kept on the payment, when somebody takes it — emailed that figure now, or none while the fee is not yet known (#641). `WHILE_WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT` — on a game `WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT` (#625): nobody had paid, the yes is withdrawn, the leaver's hold is let go, and the payer's time runs on — the game is `SEAT_OPEN` with `filling_again` on the others' Home. So it is on a game already `filling_again`: the yes is withdrawn.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` or `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE`. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once.**

EditGroupRequest.title: EditGroupRequest
EditGroupRequest.description:
The Owner saves *Edit group* — the New group form's Name and Who can join
cards, **both as the form holds them**. The home club is not here: it never
changes (``docs/adr/0183`` §2).

group.description: The group as its page reads it, after the save.

admitted.title: Admitted
admitted.description: Everybody the switch to `ANYONE` admitted, **in the order they asked** — the Edit screen shows them. Empty for every other save.

EditedGroupResponse.title: EditedGroupResponse
EditedGroupResponse.description: The group as *Edit group* left it, and who the save let in.

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: The page, **oldest first inside it**. Empty when `before_seq` was 1 — there is nothing before the beginning.

people.title: People
people.description: Every author and every actor on this page, resolved once and ordered by id. **Not the roster and not a superset of it** — a page names only what is on it, so merge these into the `people` you already hold rather than replacing them. Empty when `entries` is.

EntryPageResponse.title: EntryPageResponse
EntryPageResponse.description:
One page backward. **No header, and no instant** — but the page's own faces.

`people` is not a header: it says nothing about the room and nothing about
who is in it. It is the one thing the detail read could not have given a
client for this page, because the people a page names are not the members.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response, on both API surfaces.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for this exact failure. The only half of the envelope a client may branch on.
code.title: Code

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic. Never the copy shown to a user — that is the client's, chosen from the code.
message.title: Message

trace_id.description: This request's identifier, also returned on the X-Request-ID header. Ties a client-side failure to a server log without logging a payload.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

details.description: Structured context for this code, when the code defines any.
details.title: Details

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FactorResponse.title: FactorResponse
FactorResponse.description:
One evidence category's row: what it says, and which way it pulled.

``direction`` is one of ``up`` / ``down`` / ``neutral``, computed by the
engine from that category's own evidence against the final estimate. The
client never derives it — a client-side arrow is a second opinion about the
arithmetic, and two clients would eventually hold two of them.

FailureReason.title: FailureReason
FailureReason.description: Why a share could not be held (the mechanics §12.2, §19).

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant every row and deadline here was read against.

badge.title: Badge
badge.description: The tab's badge: the Seats to fill rows.

seats_to_fill.title: Seats To Fill
seats_to_fill.description: Every rescue in the group the reader fits — the pair rule, the kind their intent wants, free for the hour in their week, no game of theirs then, within their Games & money — **soonest first**, before or after the cut-off. Never a game still filling: that is the deck's. *You're In* is `GET /players/me/live-yeses`.

FillInResponse.title: FillInResponse
FillInResponse.description: A group's **Fill in** tab for one sport: *Seats to fill* (#545).

ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest
ForgotPasswordRequest.description: *Forgot password?*: the address to send a link and a code to.

home_club.title: Home Club
home_club.description: The group's home club, listed first.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: How far it is from the poster; `null` with no Location area.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: The latest the post can fill.

courts.title: Courts
courts.description: How many courts of the sport are free then.

fits_free.title: Fits Free
fits_free.description: Its own *n free*: the poster's best fits free at this hour.

FreeCourtSchema.title: FreeCourtSchema
FreeCourtSchema.description: One *Free courts* row: a club and hour the post could be made at.

GameKind.title: GameKind
GameKind.description:
Whether this game is evidence about how well anybody plays.

**Stamped at the plan and never derived at the end.** ADR-0049's fourth
rejected option is the reason: *a friendly is a thing people choose*, and
reclassifying a counted game because nobody typed a score hands a player the
exact evening they said they did not want, and gives one word two meanings —
what you chose, and what you failed to record.

GameListResponse.title: GameListResponse
GameListResponse.description:
Your games, newest arrangement first.

**One list and not several.** A game awaiting an entry, one awaiting an
answer and one that is over are one thing at three moments of its life,
and splitting them would make the client's shelves the platform's opinion
about which of them matters.

``read_at`` is the instant every standing and deadline here was folded
against. It travels so a client's countdowns and the standings beside them
cannot come from two different readings of the clock.

GameOutcome.title: GameOutcome
GameOutcome.description:
How one counted game went for the person the record is about. **Two.**

*Unscored* is not a third value: a game nobody agreed a score for produced no
outcome for anybody, and the absence is spelled by not being in the run at
all (``docs/adr/0137``).

**A second spelling of ``games``' own ``Outcome``**, mapped at the adapter
that reads it — which is the shape ``matchmaking``'s ``GameResult`` already
takes for the same two words, and this context's standing rule about
borrowing another context's domain types (``docs/adr/0159``). The risk is the
same one ``OnCourtVerdict`` carries and it is answered the same way:
``tests/unit/test_player_record_skill.py`` fails the build if the two
vocabularies stop agreeing.

GamePairingAtStakeSchema.title: GamePairingAtStakeSchema
GamePairingAtStakeSchema.description:
What a **counted** game on this court would do to your Level.

The rating engine's own update rule read forward, **side against side** —
the pair the result will deliver if the game is played, and the same pair
for everybody on your side.

sigma_group.title: Sigma Group
sigma_group.description: The confidence is part of the claim, so it crosses with it.

assumption.title: Assumption
assumption.description: What the provisional figure assumed, as a code the client renders in its own words. Null when nothing was assumed — which, on a game, is always.

GamePairingForecastSchema.title: GamePairingForecastSchema
GamePairingForecastSchema.description:
How even this court's game is forecast to be, **read in your direction**.

``provisional`` travels inside the forecast rather than beside it, on the
engine's own rule: the failure guarded against is a screen showing the
number without its caveat. **It is never `true` on a game today** — a
line-up is frozen at the plan, so no side is short — and the field is kept
because the shape is the court's. When a seat can be open, the answer is
*omitted*, never provisional.

GamePairingRangeSchema.title: GamePairingRangeSchema
GamePairingRangeSchema.description:
The likely range a seat's Level sits in — μ ± σ as RacketSkill published it.

Named for its surface rather than reusing the card's ``LikelyRangeSchema``:
a second class of that name would not shadow the card's in the contract, it
would rename it (``docs/adr/0159``'s rule, one context over).

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant the game's standing was folded at and the pairing computed against.

forecast.description: How even the game is forecast to be, in your direction. **Omitted when the pairing cannot be computed**, and always together with `split`.

split.description: The evidence behind `pct`: between what and what, on the scale you already read Levels on. **Omitted together with `forecast`.**

at_stake.description: What a counted result would do to your Level. **Omitted on a friendly** — meaningless rather than unavailable — and omitted where you hold no rating in this sport, or nobody on the other side does. A side with one unrated seat is priced over the people on it who are rated, because that is what the result will do. Never a pair of zeros.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: One row per seat whose person holds a rating in this sport, in the court's own order. Somebody unrated is simply not here.

GamePairingResponse.title: GamePairingResponse
GamePairingResponse.description:
What this platform makes of your court, computed when you asked.

**Read beside the game and stored nowhere.** Everything here is as-of-now
and means what a card means *because this game has not happened*; the route
refuses once it has. Nothing on `GET /games` changes: a seat there still
carries a name and nothing else.

**Three blocks, and each is omitted on its own ground.** `forecast` and
`split` go together — one computation — and are omitted when the pairing
cannot be computed: somebody on the court holds no rating in the sport, or
a seat could not be priced. There is no reason beside the absence; draw
nothing and say nothing. `at_stake` is omitted on a friendly, where a
counted result is *meaningless rather than unavailable*, and where the rule
has nothing to move or nothing to price against — you hold no rating in
the sport, or nobody across the net does. `seats` names the Level of
everybody the platform holds one for, and a court with an unrated member
still names the rated ones.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level, as RacketSkill published it.

band.title: Band
band.description: The Level band's published name, as a key — RacketSkill's own vocabulary, exactly as the player card and the record print it. The band's numeric edges are **not** here: they are not a second range to compare `range` against.

range.description: The likely range their Level sits in, as the play card ships it. **The client computes nothing** — not this from `confidence`, and not a band from `level`.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure the platform is, as a whole percentage — `rating`'s own figure and never re-derived here.

GamePairingSeatSchema.title: GamePairingSeatSchema
GamePairingSeatSchema.description:
One seat on the court and the Level of the person in it.

**This is not a card**, and it is not the seat on `GET /games` either — that
one carries a name and nothing else (``docs/adr/0141``), and it is
untouched. What is here is the four figures a record's skill panel and a
player card already publish, read beside the game for as long as the game
has not happened.

GamePairingSplitSchema.title: GamePairingSplitSchema
GamePairingSplitSchema.description:
The two side strengths the forecast was read from, **in your direction**.

`your_side` is yours wherever you sit, and `gap` is `your_side − their_side`
— **signed and served**, so two readers on opposite sides see the sign flip
and neither subtracts two rounded figures the engine subtracted unrounded.
A side's strength is not the mean of the people on it, which is why these
are numbers only the engine has.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: The booking this game was opened for. **A game is opened only by a booking**, so every game has one — and its chat is the room filed under the same `booking_id` in `GET /conversations`.

kind.description: Whether this evening is evidence. **Chosen when the game was arranged and never derived at the end** — a game nobody scored stays counted, because a friendly is a thing people choose.

window.description: How soon the week this was arranged for came round. ``null`` on every booked game, which has an hour instead.

standing.description: What this game is at the instant it was read. **Derived from the record and the clock, never stored**, so it is right for the whole gap between a deadline and anything noticing.

planned_at.title: Planned At
planned_at.description: When the court was booked and this became a game

played_at.title: Played At
played_at.description: When somebody said it happened. **The entry carries the moment** — there is no booking and no calendar, so this is the moment of the entry itself. ``null`` while nobody has said so.

entry_closes_at.title: Entry Closes At
entry_closes_at.description: When *we played* stops being sayable, and a full game nobody recorded reads `PLAYED_NO_SCORE`. ``null`` once somebody has said it happened, and ``null`` on a game that was called off — the window no longer matters, and a card that shelved itself by it would stay for eight days.

called_off_at.title: Called Off At
called_off_at.description: When it was called off — at the club's cut-off with a seat open, or by the club taking the court back (``docs/adr/0163``). ``null`` unless the standing is `CALLED_OFF`; then the act's own instant, which is what the ending card is shelved from — a day later, as `played_at` and `entry_closes_at` already shelve the other endings. Who is `called_off_by`.

called_off_by.description: The player who called it off, and their name (``docs/adr/0172`` §4). ``null`` on every standing but `CALLED_OFF` — and on a booked game called off by its cut-off or its club, which nobody did.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: The court, in the order the booking handed it over

score.description: The agreed score. ``null`` until something settles on one — including while a lone score is still waiting, because a score nobody has answered yet is not the result, and on a `DISPUTED` game, whose two scores named different winners. Two scores naming the same winner settle on the **closer**: the smaller margin in games, and on a tie the first put up.

outcome.description: Win or loss **for you**. ``null`` for every standing but a confirmed one: a game nobody scored moves nobody's Level and has no outcome to give anybody.

proposals.title: Proposals
proposals.description: The scores on the table, **side A's first and never in the order they arrived**. Empty unless the game is awaiting an answer: before that nobody has entered one, and after it the ending is on `standing` — a confirmed score is `score`, and a disputed or unscored game is an evening, not a transcript of the argument. Two entries **is** the disagreement, and either side may agree with the other's. Always empty on a For fun game, whose score is the result the moment it is put up: it asks nobody.

attendance.title: Attendance
attendance.description: Everybody somebody on the court said was not here yet, in the court's order (#657) — **empty on an ordinary game**, where everybody arrived on time and nobody tapped anything. While anybody is `WAITING` the game is `NOT_HERE_YET`; anybody `DIDNT_COME` or `CLAIMED` makes it `DIDNT_COME`, and no score is taken beside either.

GameSchema.title: GameSchema
GameSchema.description: One game, its court, and what it is right now.

GameSide.title: GameSide
GameSide.description: Which side of the net. **Two, and the game names one of them.**

GameStanding.title: GameStanding
GameStanding.description: The nine standings, as codes. A client's words are the client's own.

games_per_week.title: Games Per Week
games_per_week.description: Games a week, Monday to Sunday, from 1 to 7.

most_ill_pay_grosze.title: Most Ill Pay Grosze
most_ill_pay_grosze.description: The most one game's share may cost, in grosze — one of `most_ill_pay_choices_grosze` — or `null` for *off*.

GamesAndMoneyRequest.title: GamesAndMoneyRequest
GamesAndMoneyRequest.description:
Both values, as the screen saves them on every tap. **Types only**: a
value the form does not offer is refused by the domain, with a code naming
what it offers.

games_per_week.title: Games Per Week
games_per_week.description: Once this many games are booked in a week (Monday to Sunday), the deck deals nothing more for it.

most_ill_pay_grosze.title: Most Ill Pay Grosze
most_ill_pay_grosze.description: Cards whose share is above this, in grosze, are never dealt; `null` is *off* — every card is shown.

most_ill_pay_choices_grosze.title: Most Ill Pay Choices Grosze
most_ill_pay_choices_grosze.description: The ceilings offered beside *Off*, in grosze.

GamesAndMoneyResponse.title: GamesAndMoneyResponse
GamesAndMoneyResponse.description:
You › Account › **Games & money**: the player's two limits, and what the
form offers so the client holds neither range.

Gender.title: Gender
Gender.description:
What a player says about themselves — self-declared, freely changed.

Per person and never per sport, which is what keeps it on ``PlayerProfile``
rather than beside a rating (ADR-0089's cardinality, unchanged).

This is **a statement about which games a player wishes to be put in**, not
a ruling by the platform on who anybody is. A player whose identity is not on
this list picks the answer that puts them where they want to be, or takes
``PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`` and is paired only with players who asked for anybody.
The platform adjudicates nothing.

GenderPreference.title: GenderPreference
GenderPreference.description:
Who a player is willing to be matched with — durable, never per game.

**Durable because the gate is mutual.** It has to be evaluated against a
player when somebody *else's* game is being made and they are not present,
and a setting made at the moment could not bind that direction at all.

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` — *Join* admits at once (*anyone can join*); `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE` — *Ask to join* leaves a request for the Owner (*Karol approves joins*).

owner_name.title: Owner Name
owner_name.description: The Owner's **whole Name**, never the nickname — who answers a request, for the *approves joins* line. **No first name is cut from it, here or by a client**: a sentence naming somebody uses the whole Name (`docs/adr/0171` §4), so the line reads *Karol Nowak approves joins* and the row truncates it as it truncates any line. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — and **always `null` on an official group**, which has no Owner: its line names `administrator_name`.

administrator_name.title: Administrator Name
administrator_name.description: **An official group's** *approves joins* line: the whole name the club gave the Administrator running it now — *Administrator Marta Wójcik approves joins* — cut by nobody, as `owner_name` is. `null` while nobody runs it, and **always `null` on a player group**, whose line names `owner_name`.

is_administrator.title: Is Administrator
is_administrator.description: Whether **the reader** runs this official group. Their tap is **Join**, never *Ask to join*: they are admitted at once whatever `join_policy` says — they would otherwise be asking themselves. Always `false` on a player group.

relation.description: `MEMBER` — the reader is in it (*you're in*); `REQUESTED` — they asked and their request is waiting (*requested · waiting*); `NONE` — neither, and *Join* or *Ask to join* is the tap. **A declined request reads `NONE`**: nothing tells them it was declined, and they may ask again.

GroupAtClubSchema.title: GroupAtClubSchema
GroupAtClubSchema.description: A group inside a club's card, with what it is to the reader.

segments.title: Segments
segments.description: The segments the reader's Play intent shows, Competitive first — **empty while they have declared no intent for the sport**, which is the one question that replaces the deck.

games_badge.title: Games Badge
games_badge.description: The tab's badge: cards where somebody is already In with the reader, across the segments.

capped_weeks.title: Capped Weeks
capped_weeks.description: Weeks within the deck's fortnight at the reader's games per week — *your 2 games this week are booked*. None of their games is dealt.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: This segment's cards in the order dealt. **A card owed to the reader comes first** — the new game a club's cancel owed them, soonest first among two, with no mark (#673). Then seats open after the reader's yes (fewest first), then seat open › challenge › pick, then the soonest deadline, then the best forecast; the same people only at their best hour.

GroupDeckResponse.title: GroupDeckResponse
GroupDeckResponse.description: A group's **Games** tab for one sport and segment.

GroupKind.title: GroupKind
GroupKind.description:
The two kinds of Group (``docs/adr/0183`` §1), and every rule that differs
between them says which it binds rather than reading a null.

A **player group** has an Owner who created it and plays whatever its
members are rated in. An **official group** belongs to a club, has **no
Owner** — one Administrator runs it — and **declares** its sports and the
size of the WhatsApp group it mirrors (§3).

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole Name, never the nickname. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — the member keeps their seat.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — draw their initials.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in the sport asked for, as RacketSkill published it. Always present: somebody not rated in it is not listed.

player_score.title: Player Score
player_score.description: Their published Player Score, 0–100 — the figure their record and a player card print. **Omitted for somebody the platform has watched nothing of**, never `0`: no record is not a bad one.

is_owner.title: Is Owner
is_owner.description: Whether they own the group — the row the **admin** tag is drawn on in a player group.

is_administrator.title: Is Administrator
is_administrator.description: Whether they run this **official** group as its Administrator, and joined it as a player — the row the **admin** tag is drawn on in an official group, second after the reader as an Owner is. Always `false` on a player group.

joined_at.title: Joined At

GroupMemberSchema.description: One row of Members, for one sport — *Padel 2,71 · score 92*.

Empty when nobody in the group is rated in it.

GroupPersonSchema.description: A member's face — **a name and a photograph, and nothing else**.

joined_at.description: When they joined — this stay. The app prints *this week* within seven days, and the date after.

GroupPlayerSchema.title: GroupPlayerSchema
GroupPlayerSchema.description:
One player on an official group's page — rows are not tappable, and
nobody can be removed.

GroupRelation.title: GroupRelation
GroupRelation.description:
What a group is to the person reading it (``docs/adr/0183`` §9): they
are in it, they have asked and their Join request is waiting, or neither.

**A declined request reads as ``NONE``** — the request is gone, and nothing
tells them it was declined (``docs/adr/0183`` §7).

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

link.title: Link
link.description: The Group link: the public site's address, `/join/` and the group's code. **It never changes** — not on a rename, a policy change or a handover.

is_owner.title: Is Owner
is_owner.description: Whether the reader is the group's Owner. Always `false` on an official group, which has none.

declared_sports.title: Declared Sports
declared_sports.description: **An official group's** declared sports, in the registry's order — what it plays, so the sport filter narrows to the ones the reader is rated in among these, and a reader rated in none of them is shown what to add. **Omitted on a player group**, which plays whatever its members are rated in.

rated_by_sport.title: Rated By Sport
rated_by_sport.description: **Every sport**, in the registry's order — one the group has no dot for too, because the reader may be rated in it and open it.

member_faces.title: Member Faces
member_faces.description: The Info tab's members row: **up to five** faces of everybody but the reader, in the Members list's order — the Owner, then newest joined first. A block hides nobody here, as it hides nobody in the list it opens. Empty for a reader alone (`member_count` 1), whose row draws their own face. `member_count` is the group's, so its *+N* counts everybody.

administrator_name.title: Administrator Name
administrator_name.description: **An official group's** *approves joins* line, as a club's card says it: the whole Name of the Administrator running it now. **`null` while it needs an administrator** — the line then names the home club, *Ogrody 33 approves joins*, and requests wait for a handover — and **always `null` on a player group**, whose line names its Owner.

is_administrator.title: Is Administrator
is_administrator.description: Whether **the reader** runs this official group — who joined it as a player: *you approve joins*, answered from the administrator profile. Always `false` on a player group.

GroupResponse.title: GroupResponse
GroupResponse.description: A group, as one of its members opens it.

rated_count.title: Rated Count
rated_count.description: How many members hold a Skill rating in it.

first_rated.title: First Rated
first_rated.description: The first members to join who are rated in it, in joining order — **at most as many as the sport seats**, the faces that fill its seats.

GroupSportSchema.title: GroupSportSchema
GroupSportSchema.description: One sport's *N of M* for the Games tab.

waiting_count.title: Waiting Count
waiting_count.description: How many Join requests wait on it — the queue the handover gave.

HandoverSchema.title: HandoverSchema
HandoverSchema.description:
A group the club handed this account that it has not been told about —
*Ogrody 33 made you the administrator of Ogrody 33 Club*.

group_ids.title: Group Ids
group_ids.description: The `group_id` of each handover the sheet named, from `/users/me`'s `profiles.handovers`. A group handed on meanwhile, told about already or not theirs is stepped over.

HandoversSeenRequest.title: HandoversSeenRequest
HandoversSeenRequest.description: The groups the sheet told the Administrator about (``docs/adr/0192``).

clubs.title: Clubs
clubs.description: Nearest first, then by name — or A–Z for a reader with no Location area.

next_page.title: Next Page
next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or `null` when this was the last.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: The booking — the same id the game had while it filled. `GET /bookings/{id}` for its details.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The ordinary Game it opened: the result is told and agreed on `/games/{id}/result`, and its room in `GET /conversations` carries this id. `null` on a game that waited for a payment and was never booked — there is no Game, and no room.

pool_id.title: Pool Id
pool_id.description: The pool it filled in — a group's id.

status.description: `BOOKED` — full and booked, its hour still ahead. `NEEDS_RESULT` — its hour has come and nobody has said it happened. `CONFIRM_THE_RESULT` — a score is on the table. `COUNTED` — a score is agreed. `UNCOUNTED` — they played and no score is agreed: two scores named different winners (no `uncounted_reason`), or one of the reasons `uncounted_reason` names. `PLAYED_NO_SCORE` — full at its hour, and nobody recorded it before the entry window closed: played for everybody on it, and no Level moves. `CALLED_OFF` — it will not be played; `called_off_reason` says why. `SEAT_OPEN` — somebody left and the seat is offered (`open_seats`); before the cut-off (`money.free_to_leave_until`) *fills by then or the game is off and everyone is refunded*, after it *the game goes ahead*. A game whose hour comes with a seat still open is `UNCOUNTED` with `uncounted_reason` `SEAT_EMPTY`. **`WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT`** (#625; Q111) — full, and one player's share was refused when it filled: *Waiting for one payment · until `payment_due_by` · Nobody pays until it's in*. Nobody paid, there is no Game and no court given, and it asks nothing of the reader (`needs_you` is `false`); to the payer it reads *Confirm your payment by `your_payment_due_by`* — *Fix your card by …* before the cut-off (`time_to`, #638) — beside their *To confirm* row. Paid in time it is `BOOKED`; out of time it is `SEAT_OPEN` with `filling_again` — and so is a game one of the others left meanwhile. **`SEAT_OPEN` with `filling_again`** (Q106) — a full game that went back to filling before it was booked: a payment it waited for did not come in time, or a seat opened while it waited — a player left, their week filled, or two players stopped fitting. Nobody paid, there is no Game and no court, and it asks nothing of the reader (`needs_you` is `false`): *1 seat open · books when it's full · nobody paid*. It is in the reader's live yeses too, where *Withdraw* (`DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes`, the same id) takes it off their Home. Full again, it reads `BOOKED`; `CALLED_OFF` if its book-by passes first. No club confirms a game: nothing on Home waits for a club's answer (#669).

called_off_reason.description: Why a `CALLED_OFF` game will not be played — `null` on every other status. `BOOK_BY_PASSED` — a game that went back to filling reached its book-by before it was full again: nobody paid. `COURT_HOUR_LOST` — a game that went back to filling lost its court to another game before it was full again — or before the payment it waited for came in: nobody paid, and its players are dealt a new card first. `PAYMENT_NOT_IN_TIME` — a payment the game waited for did not come in time and it could no longer fill: the book-by had come (#625). Nobody paid. `SHORT_AT_THE_CUT_OFF` — a seat that opened before the club's cut-off was still empty at it: everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`); read off the clock from the cut-off on. `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` — the club cancelled it, with its reason (`club_cancel_reason`): everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`), it is on nobody's record, and they are dealt a new card first (#547).

club_cancel_reason.description: Why the club cancelled a `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` game — `WEATHER`, `REPAIR`, `DOUBLE_BOOKING` or `OTHER` (no reason given). `null` on every other game.

uncounted_reason.description: Why an `UNCOUNTED` game is uncounted with nobody disagreeing about a score — `null` otherwise. `SEAT_EMPTY` — its hour came with a seat open: somebody left after the cut-off and nobody took the seat. No Level moved, and nothing is on the record of those who stayed. `DIDNT_COME` — somebody was tapped *isn't here yet* at the court and never arrived (#657; `GET /games` — `attendance`): the game takes no score and never counts. For a day it is provisional — their *I was there*, confirmed by somebody else on the court, makes them Came late and the game carries on.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats a leaver left open — the dashed tiles; nought unless `SEAT_OPEN`. The sides list the seats still held. On a game `filling_again`, the seats nobody is In on, the sides listing everybody In now.

needs_you.title: Needs You
needs_you.description: One of the games that need the reader: a result to enter, the other side's score waiting on their agreement, or a seat open in their booked game — never a game `filling_again`, which asks nothing of them.

filling_again.title: Filling Again
filling_again.description: A full game that went back to filling before it was booked (#625, Q106) — `SEAT_OPEN` while it fills, nobody paid; `CALLED_OFF` once its book-by passes, or its court goes, before it is full again. `false` on every booked game.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court — *Court 2*. `null` on a game that was never booked, which no court was given.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: The court's kind — *Court 2 · indoor* — which follows a move (Q122). `null` with `court_name`.

payment_due_by.title: Payment Due By
payment_due_by.description: When the payment the game waits for is due — *Waiting for one payment · until 14:40 · Nobody pays until it's in* (#625; Q111): a share was refused, and its player's seat is theirs alone until then. Never names whose payment it is. `null` unless `WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT`. Like `free_to_leave_until`, the line switches by itself at this instant.

your_payment_due_by.title: Your Payment Due By
your_payment_due_by.description: **The reader's own** refused share and their time to pay — *Confirm your payment by 14:40*, or before the cut-off *Fix your card by 14:40* (`time_to`, #638) — while it runs, on a game waiting for it or one gone back to filling meanwhile (#625). The payment is their *To confirm* row's (`GET /players/me/payments-to-confirm`). **A rescuer whose share was refused** reads, from outside, the seat kept for them alone until then (#640) — *Fix your card by 14:40 to take the seat*, or after the cut-off *Confirm your payment by 14:40* — offered to nobody else meanwhile. `null` for everybody else, and from the moment it runs out.

time_to.description: What the time to `payment_due_by` and `your_payment_due_by` is for (#638; Q113). `FIX_THE_CARD` — the hold was refused **before the club's cut-off**, where nothing is taken, only held: the payer reads *Fix your card by 14:40 to keep your seat* — nothing is paid now — and the time never runs past the cut-off. `PAY` — refused from the cut-off on, where the money is taken at once: *Confirm your payment by 14:40*. The others read *Waiting for one payment* either way. `null` while neither is set.

HomeGameSchema.title: HomeGameSchema
HomeGameSchema.description: One card on Home: a game the reader booked.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant every status and money line here was folded against. Switch a card's line at `free_to_leave_until` from this clock.

needing_you.title: Needing You
needing_you.description: Home's badge — the games that need the reader: the cards with `needs_you`, and every payment they have to confirm (`GET /players/me/payments-to-confirm`), a game still filling whose seat is theirs until somebody else takes it.

games.title: Games
games.description: The reader's booked games — and their full games waiting for one payment, or gone back to filling — **soonest first**, and only what Home draws: **every live game** (waiting for a payment, booked, with a seat open, waiting on its result or on an answer to a score), **every game that ended less than a day after its hour's end**, and **any game that needs the reader** (`needs_you`). Nothing older is sent; its details (`GET /bookings/{id}`) still read it. A game a Classic play challenge opened is not here.

HomeResponse.title: HomeResponse
HomeResponse.description: **Home**: the reader's games from the moment they fill.

HomeStatus.title: HomeStatus
HomeStatus.description: What a game on Home is, right now (the mechanics §14.1).

InProgressAssessmentResponse.title: InProgressAssessmentResponse
InProgressAssessmentResponse.description:
One unfinished run: which assessment, and which sport it is for.

Carries no question, no result and no progress. A caller reading this is
deciding *where to send the player*; it re-reads the run it routes to, and
that read is the one that reproduces the outstanding question.

InProgressAssessmentsResponse.title: InProgressAssessmentsResponse
InProgressAssessmentsResponse.description:
Every unfinished run this player holds — empty when they hold none.

Empty is the ordinary answer for a new account and for a player who has
finished everything they started, so it is a 200 with an empty list rather
than a 404 or the singular form's 204.

Ordered by the sport registry, so a caller that wants one run can take the
first entry.

InvitationByTokenRequest.title: InvitationByTokenRequest
InvitationByTokenRequest.description:
The token off an invitation's link. In a body rather than a path, so it
is in no access log.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name the club typed.

state.description: `valid`, `expired` (ask the club to send a new one), `used`, or `locked` — five wrong codes.

InvitationByTokenResponse.title: InvitationByTokenResponse
InvitationByTokenResponse.description:
What a link opens, before anything is set: the email *Set your
password* locks its field to, whom it greets, and whether it still
works.

InvitationLinkState.title: InvitationLinkState
InvitationLinkState.description:
Whether an invitation's link still works — the credential's standing,
under a name of its own on the wire (``Standing`` is a challenge's).

InvitationPasswordRequest.title: InvitationPasswordRequest
InvitationPasswordRequest.description:
*Set your password*, and **exactly one** of what opens the way to it:
the `token` from the email's link, or the `ticket` a claimed code returned.

The password carries no bound here: the rule every account shares — 8 to
128 characters with a letter and a digit — is refused as
`password_too_weak` naming the field. Sending both or neither of `token`
and `ticket` is the one refusal here that is a `422`.

JoinPolicy.title: JoinPolicy
JoinPolicy.description:
Who gets in (``docs/adr/0183`` §7).

**Anyone** admits a player the moment they join, and is the default the New
group form opens on. **People I approve** turns a join into a Join request
its Owner answers.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole Name, never the nickname. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — the member keeps their seat.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — draw their initials.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**.

levels.title: Levels
levels.description: **Every sport they are rated in**, in the registry's order, each with its Level — *Padel 2,44 · Tennis 2,60*. Empty for somebody rated in nothing.

JoinRequestSchema.title: JoinRequestSchema
JoinRequestSchema.description:
A Join request as the Owner sees it: who is asking — ``player_id`` is the
id to approve or decline — and what they play. **No Player Score**: the
request card is club 20's everywhere.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: Everybody waiting to be let in, **in the order they asked** — *Want to join · N*. Empty when nobody is waiting.

clubs.title: Clubs
clubs.description: Nearest first, then by name — or A–Z for a reader with no Location area. Empty when nothing matched.

next_page.title: Next Page
next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or `null` when this was the last.

read_as.description: What the text was read as. `LINK` — it held `/join/` and a code, and the answer is exactly that group; **`LINK` with no clubs is *nothing at that link***, a link that leads nowhere. `TEXT` — matched against clubs, districts and group names; `TEXT` with no clubs is *no match*.

Leaving.title: Leaving
Leaving.description:
What *Leave the game* does, by when it is pressed (the mechanics §13) —
said on the details before, and answered by the act after.

kind.description: `BEFORE_THE_CUT_OFF` — *Nothing is taken: the hold on your card is let go. Your seat is offered to others. On your record only if the game is then called off.* (Q113) `AFTER_THE_CUT_OFF` — *Your seat is offered to others. If someone takes it, you get 38,24 zł back (40 zł less the 1,76 zł kept on your payment); if nobody does, you won't. On your record if nobody takes it.* — with no figure and no clause while the fee kept is not yet known (#641). `WHILE_WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT` — the game waits for one payment (#625): *Nobody has paid yet. Leaving withdraws your yes.* The same words the departure answers with.

refund_grosze.title: Refund Grosze
refund_grosze.description: After the cut-off, what comes back if somebody takes the seat — the share less **exactly the fee kept on the reader's own payment**, to the grosz (#641); nought when nobody paid. `null` before the cut-off, when nothing is taken and nothing comes back (#637), and **while that fee is not yet known** — a club on its own negotiated pricing is told it after the share is taken: no figure and no clause, never an estimate.

card_fee_grosze.title: Card Fee Grosze
card_fee_grosze.description: After the cut-off, exactly what was kept on the reader's payment — *1,76 zł* on a 40 zł share paid by a business card — the provider's own figure, as the refund's receipt will say it. `null` wherever `refund_grosze` is.

LeavingSchema.title: LeavingSchema
LeavingSchema.description: What *Leave the game* would cost now (the mechanics §13).

LevelRangeSchema.title: LevelRangeSchema
LevelRangeSchema.description: A range of Levels, both bounds included.

v.title: V
v.description: The envelope version, **carried from the first frame**. `1` today. A client parses the shape it shipped with until that build is gone from phones, so this is what a later shape is told apart by.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: The room that moved. It is the room this stream is for — a stream carries one room and there is deliberately no second stream for the Chats list.

last_seq.title: Last Seq
last_seq.description: How long the room is now. **News, not a cursor.** Fetch from your own high-water mark, never from this number: a client that paged from here would reintroduce exactly the hole the nudge exists to close. `0` is a room where nothing has landed yet, which a stream opened on a freshly-opened room genuinely reports.

LiveNudgeSchema.title: LiveNudgeSchema
LiveNudgeSchema.description:
**The whole live contract: a nudge, and nothing else on the wire.**

``docs/adr/0147`` §3. One of these is written into
``GET /conversations/{id}/stream`` whenever the room moves, and one is
written the moment the stream opens carrying the room's current `last_seq`.

**It carries no content, ever.** Not a message, not a system line, not a plan
slot. On receiving one, fetch from **your own** high-water mark through the
