ordinary read path — never from `last_seq`. That is what makes a dropped
frame free: the next nudge repairs it, because your cursor is yours.

**Which also means there is nothing here to render.** Whether the UI may draw
something it did not read from the authenticated read path stops being a rule
anybody keeps and becomes a thing this shape cannot express.

**The declaration is generated and the emission is not, and that hole is
named** (``docs/adr/0147`` §7). `make openapi` publishes this model into
`components.schemas`, the client generates **this type** from it, and the
drift and freshness checks cover the declaration. The *operation's* 200 comes
out of `openapi-typescript` as `unknown`, because a stream body is an
`itemSchema` that generator has no shape for — so the client's live port
parses each frame as this type by name, which is still generated and still
never hand-written. **What no check covers is the emission** — a stream body is
not a response model, and nothing type-checks the route against its own
annotation. The mitigation is structural rather than hoped for: the route
declares this model as its stream item, so the framework validates and
serialises every frame **through this model** before it reaches the wire. The
hole is narrowed, not closed, and the residual risk is that of a shape three
fields wide.

v.title: V
v.description: The envelope version, **the same `1` a nudge carries and unbumped by this frame's arrival**. A named event an installed client does not listen for never reaches it, so nothing about the shape it parses has changed.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: The room this is about — the room this stream is for

player_ids.title: Player Ids
player_ids.description: Who is typing **right now**, never including you. A list because a group chat has more than one possible typist; draw one indicator either way. **Empty means nobody is**, which is how an indicator goes away.

LiveTypingSchema.title: LiveTypingSchema
LiveTypingSchema.description:
**Somebody is typing**, and it is the second frame on the wire.

``docs/adr/0156``. It arrives when the answer changes and not on a tick, so a
room where nobody is typing produces nothing at all.

**It carries no `last_seq` and moves no sequence.** A typing frame is not an
entry: nothing was appended, nothing was locked, and the gapless allocator
behind `seq` was never asked for a number. A client must not advance any
cursor on one, and there is nothing here it could advance it to.

**It carries no name.** Fill names from the membership you are already
holding, exactly as every system line does — which is why a corrected
name fixes the indicator without a frame being re-sent.

**An empty list is the clear**, and it is the only clear there is: nobody
sends *stopped*, and the server reports whoever's heartbeat has not expired.
A room whose last typist's app was killed reports nobody within seconds,
through the same field and with nothing special about it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

pool_id.title: Pool Id
pool_id.description: The pool the game was dealt in — a group's id.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start. Every game is one hour.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What this player is charged if the game fills, in grosze.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: The latest moment the game can fill; past it the yes lapses.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: The kind of court the game promises — `true` *Indoor*, `false` *Outdoor* — when every free court it could be booked on is of that kind; `null` when they are mixed, which promises neither (Q122). The same rule as the deck card's `indoor`. Shown, never chosen by.

LiveYesSchema.title: LiveYesSchema
LiveYesSchema.description: One yes on a game that has not filled.

LiveYesesResponse.title: LiveYesesResponse
LiveYesesResponse.description:
You › Payments' **LIVE YESES**: every yes of the reader's on a game that
has not filled, across groups, soonest game first.

LocationAreaResource.title: LocationAreaResource
LocationAreaResource.description:
Where a player plays.

**What is sent and what is kept are not the same number.** A client sends the
fix its device gave it; the platform rounds to roughly a kilometre before
anything is recorded, and it is the rounded pair that comes back here. The
precise fix is never stored and never shareable
(``../../../../CONTEXT.md`` — *Location area*).

accuracy_m.title: Accuracy M
accuracy_m.description: The fix's own stated accuracy, in metres — the radius the phone says the true position lies within. Allowed for up to 200 m.

LocationFixSchema.title: LocationFixSchema
LocationFixSchema.description:
**One precise fix, read by the phone at the moment of the tap** and sent
with it (#657; ``docs/adr/0195`` §3). It is measured against the club's map
point and dropped: **the backend keeps only whether it was at the club**,
never the position.

name.title: Name
name.description: What this player is called — what every screen says. `null` until the naming — except on an account an invitation opened, which carries the name the club typed. The entry gate's first destination is **not named in full**: no name, or no nickname — and the naming step asks only for what is missing.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: The handle, unique across the platform, drawn as `@nickname` under the name on the You tab and nowhere else. `null` until the naming.

has_player_profile.title: Has Player Profile
has_player_profile.description: Whether this player has committed a Player profile — the fourth branch of the entry gate. Read from the profile's own event stream rather than from a projection, so it is correct immediately after the commit that creates one. False on a response that is not about the authenticated player, such as the one registration returns.

adult_attested.title: Adult Attested
adult_attested.description: Whether this account has given the Adult attestation. Every sign-up has; an account an invitation opened has not, and *Start playing* asks it first — `POST /users/me/adult-attestation`.

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description:
``/me``: the account, and **which profiles it holds**
(``docs/adr/0185`` §2) — what the entry gate reads ahead of every
onboarding destination.

Its own shape rather than more fields on :class:`UserResponse`, because the
registration's answer is about an account one line old and has no honest
value for either: it holds no profile yet, and ``/me`` is where the gate
reads them.

type.title: Type
type.description: The discriminator. Two genuinely different shapes ride one ordered stream; this is not a `kind` on one shape (`docs/adr/0148` §4).

seq.title: Seq
seq.description: This entry's place in the conversation. **Gapless and starting at 1**, so `seq` 1 is the beginning of the room — which is why there is no `has_more`. Ordering, paging, de-duplication and reconnect all key on it, and **no reader may infer loss from a gap**: the promise is the server's and nothing may depend on it.

author_id.title: Author Id
author_id.description: Who typed it — a member, since only a member may send. **Name them from the `people` on the response that carried this page**, the one list every face on it is in, so a message and a line are named the same way.

text.title: Text
text.description: Their own words, unrendered and unchanged

client_message_id.title: Client Message Id
client_message_id.description: The id the sending client generated, echoed back. It does **two jobs**: the idempotency key for a resumed send, and the key an optimistic bubble is replaced on.

MessageSchema.title: MessageSchema
MessageSchema.description: What a player typed. **Content, crossing as-is.**

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: The first character of each of the first two words, as typed, or the first two characters of a one-word name: *my raketa group* is `mr`, *Ogrody 33 Club* is `O3`. Draw it as it comes — never change its case.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: A colour **key** from 0 to 7, fixed for the group for ever — derived from its id, so a rename keeps it. Map it to your own palette; the backend never names a colour.

MonogramSchema.title: MonogramSchema
MonogramSchema.description:
The group's tile, **cut by the backend** so every client draws the same
one (``docs/adr/0183`` §5).

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

MyGroupSchema.title: MyGroupSchema
MyGroupSchema.description: A card on the reader's Groups list.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Every group the reader belongs to, **newest joined first**. Empty for a player in none.

name.title: Name
name.description: What you are called — free text, spaces allowed, **never unique**: two players may share one. Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, 2–64 characters after that. This is what every screen says about you.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: A handle: letters, digits and `. _ -`, no spaces, 2–64 characters, **unique across the platform** — refused with `nickname_already_taken` when another player holds it, admitted when it is already yours. Shown as `@nickname` under your name on your own You tab and on your record, and said nowhere else.

NameRequest.title: NameRequest
NameRequest.description:
The naming — *How should people see you?* (``docs/adr/0171`` §1–2).

Both fields, always: the naming is one act carrying both, and there is no
event for one without the other. The shape rules here are the value
objects' own, restated so the generated client type carries them — and
**the name is normalised before its bounds are checked**, exactly as
:class:`Name` normalises it, so ``"  Ania   Kowalska "`` is admitted and
recorded as ``Ania Kowalska`` and ``"   A   "`` is refused here as too
short. A bound checked on the raw string would admit the second and hand
it to the value object, which refuses it — a typed value meeting an
invariant, which is a 500 for a player's typo (``CONTEXT.md``, *Invariant
vs Unavailability*).

name.title: Name
name.description: The name as recorded: trimmed, collapsed.

NamingResponse.title: NamingResponse
NamingResponse.description:
What the naming recorded: the name as it now stands and the nickname.

Not a ``UserResponse``, deliberately — that shape carries
``has_player_profile``, a fact of another context's this write never asks
about, and ``false`` there would be a claim. The client re-reads ``/me``
before moving on (``docs/adr/0171`` §3); this is what lets it show the
normalised name back at once.

NewPasswordRequest.title: NewPasswordRequest
NewPasswordRequest.description:
The new password, and **exactly one** of what opens the way to it: the
`token` from the email's link, or the `ticket` a claimed code returned.

The password carries no bound here, deliberately: the rule every account
shares — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit — is refused as
`password_too_weak` naming the field, not as a validation error naming none.
Sending both or neither of `token` and `ticket` is a malformed request rather
than a person's mistake, and is the one refusal here that is a `422`.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who isn't here yet — somebody else on the game's court.

NoticeKind.title: NoticeKind
NoticeKind.description: Every notice a player can be told (the mechanics §17.2).

given_at.title: Given At
given_at.description: When it was given — or when the day last bundled a notice into it, which is what moves it up the list.

opens.description: `BOOKING` — the booked game's details (`GET /bookings/{game_id}`); `PROPOSAL` — a game still filling, or one that did not (`GET /proposals/{game_id}`); `DECK` — the pool's deck in the sport and kind, with this card on top.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The game it is about: its proposal's id, which its booking takes.

gathered.title: Gathered
gathered.description: How many more notices of its kind the day bundled into this one — told in its words, and pushed to nobody.

new.title: New
new.description: It reached the list since you last opened it — given, or a notice bundled into it, which moved it up — and is not your own: one the bell counts, and a row to make stand out on this visit.

your_own.title: Your Own
your_own.description: About something you did yourself and saw happen — *It's a game!* for the yes that filled the game, or the seat you took. Born seen: listed, never counted on the bell, never pushed, and never to be shown as a banner.

NoticeSchema.title: NoticeSchema
NoticeSchema.description: One notice, in the words the phone was pushed — and where a tap opens.

you_complete_it.title: You Complete It
you_complete_it.description: *You complete it* — a card needs only you. On until switched off; at most one a day, the rest bundled into it.

challenges_for_you.title: Challenges For You
challenges_for_you.description: *Challenges for you* — a member's post names you. On until switched off; at most three a day, the rest bundled into the third.

fill_in_alerts.title: Fill In Alerts
fill_in_alerts.description: *Fill in alerts* — a booked game you fit needs one more. Off until switched on; at most three a day.

NotificationChoicesSchema.title: NotificationChoicesSchema
NotificationChoicesSchema.description:
The three notices a player chooses. The nine that are always on are
no choice, and are not here.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the club offers, in the registry's order — **the sports an official group may declare**, so the form offers exactly these.

OfficialGroupClubSchema.title: OfficialGroupClubSchema
OfficialGroupClubSchema.description: The club an administrator acts for.

name.title: Name
name.description: *Same name as the WhatsApp group*: trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` or `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE`. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once.**

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group has — **required**, a whole number from 2 to 1024. It limits nothing: more players than this is allowed and honest. Refused with `whatsapp_size_invalid`, `details.field` `whatsapp_size`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the group plays — **required**, and **only the club's**. Ticking one twice is ticking it. Refused with `group_sports_required` for none, or `sport_not_offered_by_club` with the sport in `details.sport` — `details.field` `sports` either way.

OfficialGroupSettingsRequest.title: OfficialGroupSettingsRequest
OfficialGroupSettingsRequest.description:
An official group's settings, **all four as the settings screen holds
them**, recorded together or not at all.

OnCourtVerdict.title: OnCourtVerdict
OnCourtVerdict.description:
What the on-court check concluded about a photograph. **Two values.**

The third state — *nobody looked* — is the **absence** of one of these and
never a third value, which is ``docs/adr/0138``'s rule: a shield saying
*checked and passed* cannot be drawn on a photograph nothing examined, and a
value meaning *unknown* is a value somebody eventually draws a tick for.

**The words are the ones a card already carries, and they are checked
against it.** This is a second spelling of ``player_profile``'s
``PhotoReviewDecision`` on purpose — this context imports no other context's
domain types — and a second spelling that drifts is worse than an import: a
client reading a search card and a record would get two words for one fact.
``tests/unit/test_player_record_identity.py`` fails the build if the two
vocabularies stop agreeing.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The game this card is about. Post the answer to `/api/v1/sportsmanship/{game_id}`, and join it against `/api/v1/games` for the names, the sport and the date.

players.title: Players
players.description: Everybody else who was on that court, in the line-up's own order — in doubles both opponents **and** your partner, in singles the one opponent. Any of them may be left blank when you answer.

OpenCardSchema.title: OpenCardSchema
OpenCardSchema.description:
One court still waiting for this player's stars.

**Ids and nothing else.** What the people are called, which sport it was and
when it happened all come from the games list this card is drawn beside —
joined on ``game_id``, which is the same join the client already makes to
draw the game. Repeating them here would be a second copy of an evening's
description, and the day the two disagreed the card would name somebody the
game did not.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: The courts still waiting for your stars. A card appears the day after the game and stays for seven days; ignoring one costs nothing.

OpenCardsResponse.title: OpenCardsResponse
OpenCardsResponse.description:
Every card waiting for you, **soonest to expire first**.

An empty list is the ordinary answer and means nothing is waiting. It does
not distinguish *no games*, *not yet a day* and *already answered*: all three
are simply not on the list, and none of them is something a client would draw
differently.

``cards`` is **required and never absent**, empty though it usually is: a
default would emit it as optional and hand every client a list it has to
check for existence before checking for length.

Opens.title: Opens
Opens.description: The screen a notice opens on when tapped (the screens A9).

distinct_opponents.title: Distinct Opponents
distinct_opponents.description:
How many **different people** those games were against.

**A doubles partner is one of them.** *A pair is anybody you were on a court with* is the rule this platform already counts familiarity by, and a figure counting opponents alone would say that somebody who partners the same person every week spreads their games as widely as somebody who does not.

times_on_court.title: Times On Court
times_on_court.description:
How many **times they were on a court with somebody** across their counted games — the denominator of the pair, and never a count of games.

**A doubles evening contributes three.** Games were the denominator first and are only divisible in singles: one doubles game put three people on the court, so the pair read `3 of 1` and the share went over a hundred. Counting the seats opposite makes both halves the same kind of thing — *five different people across ten times on a court* — and `distinct_opponents` can never exceed it.

**It is not `skill.counted_games`, and the two will differ on this same response.** That one is *what this Level rests on*: confirmed results, in one sport, that the rating actually folded. This one is *how much have they played*: every sport, and an evening nobody agreed a score for is in it. Two honest numbers about the same person, answering two questions — do not reconcile them.

**Counted rather than every game**: a friendly was never evidence about anybody by the choice of the people who arranged it, and it is out of both halves of this pair rather than only the bottom one.

OpponentVarietySchema.title: OpponentVarietySchema
OpponentVarietySchema.description:
How widely this person spreads their games, over their **whole** record.

**Two counts and no percentage, deliberately.** The card this sits on argues
two rows above that a perfect record over nine games and one over forty are
different claims and that a bar alone hides which — so publishing a bare
share here would break the rule the card had just made about itself. Draw
both: `70 % · 14 of 20`.

**The share is yours to compute and it is one division.** Nothing is rounded
on this side and there is no banding, no floor and no tone attached — unlike
a Level's band, which is a key precisely because a client deriving it would
be a second set of drawing constants.

**This is a career statistic, not a window.** It is every counted game the
platform has recorded for them, which is what the number means: *how widely
do they spread their games*, rather than *how widely this season*. There is
no decay behind it and no horizon.

**It prices no promise.** It is not a reliability strand, it is in no
weighted score, and it neither raises nor lowers anybody's standing. It is
context for a Level — a low figure is somebody playing the same few faces
every week, whose rating may be narrow but untested.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description:
What a confirmed result says about one of the people who played.

Two values. *Unscored* is not a third: a game with no agreed result produces
**no outcome for anybody**, which is ADR-0049's *an evening, not evidence*
stated as a type — the absence has one spelling, and it is not being in the
answer.

shade.description: `BRIGHT` — everybody on the card is free together for a whole hour of it; `DIM` — all but one (never on a two-person card); `DARK` — fewer.

OverlapShade.title: OverlapShade
OverlapShade.description: How many of the card's people are free together in a cell.

method.description: The saved method, or `null` — *Not set up*.

terms_needed.title: Terms Needed
terms_needed.description: `true` when the saved card cannot be held until the player accepts the terms in force again (`POST …/terms` with no setup open): its bank moved it to another brand, or the terms were accepted in words no longer in force (`terms_version`, #637). Always `false` with no method.

terms_version.title: Terms Version
terms_version.description: The version of the terms in force.

PaymentMethodResponse.title: PaymentMethodResponse
PaymentMethodResponse.description: The player's payment method, as You › Payments draws it.

PaymentRefusal.title: PaymentRefusal
PaymentRefusal.description:
Why a seat's share could not be held — the payment's own words, spelled
here in this context's (the mechanics §12.2, §19).

setup_id.title: Setup Id
setup_id.description: The setup the phone's provider fields confirm. **Its secret is not here**: it is the answer to accepting the terms, and nothing can be saved without it.

publishable_key.title: Publishable Key
publishable_key.description: The key the provider's fields are opened with. Not a secret: it collects details and can charge nothing.

terms_version.title: Terms Version
terms_version.description: The version of the payment terms in force — the words the client must show before *Accept and continue*, and send back.

PaymentSetupResponse.title: PaymentSetupResponse
PaymentSetupResponse.description: A setup opened: what the phone opens the provider's card fields with.

terms_version.title: Terms Version
terms_version.description: The version of the words the player was shown. Anything but the terms in force is `409 payment_terms_outdated`.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: The secret the phone confirms the open setup with — its **only** appearance on any response. `null` when the terms were accepted again for the method already saved, after its bank moved it to another brand: there is nothing to confirm.

PaymentsToConfirmResponse.title: PaymentsToConfirmResponse
PaymentsToConfirmResponse.description:
*Confirm your payment to keep your seat*, every one the reader owes,
soonest game first.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Permanent id — what the profile commit carries

url.title: Url
url.description: Short-lived signed URL that reads this photo. Not a stable address: it is signed for one player, for one window, and there is no public bucket behind it.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the URL stops working. Ask for the photo again to get another; there is no way to extend one.

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about this photo, or `null` where this response carries no verdict.

**`null` is not `allowed`, and it means two different things on the two routes.** On the upload it is *the reviewer could not be asked* — our outage, and never a statement about the photograph. On the read it is *this route does not carry one*, which it never does. A client that has not been told anything must warn about nothing, and both readings collapse to that.

**A warning and nothing else.** `flagged` does not refuse, delete or hold back a photo: it is stored, it keeps its id, and a profile commit takes it like any other. The check is wrong sometimes, and the cost of being wrong is a sentence rather than a signup.

A code, not copy — the words belong to the client.

PhotoResponse.title: PhotoResponse
PhotoResponse.description:
One photo: the id a profile commit will carry, and a URL that reads it.

The same shape from the upload and from the read, so a client renders a tile
it has just filled and a tile it is restoring with one code path.

**The URL is not an identifier and must not be stored as one.** It carries a
signature and stops working at ``expires_at``; the id is what is permanent.

## The verdict crosses; the evidence does not

``review`` is the on-court check's conclusion and it is a **code**, never a
sentence: the backend emits codes and the client owns the words
(``docs/adr/0022``). ``review-note`` — the model, the prompt-set fingerprint
and the raw similarity vector — stays on the object. It is evidence for us
rather than a fact about the player, and a confidence score on the wire is an
invitation to a client that renders one.

**The upload carries it and the read does not**, which is why the field is
optional and why ``null`` is not ``allowed``. Two reasons, and neither is
that the read is harder. A warning belongs to the moment a player *chose* a
photograph; a tile being restored is a photograph they already kept, and
saying it again is a screen re-litigating a decision the player made. And the
read would have to pay for it: ``GET /photos/{id}`` proves existence and signs
a URL, and no part of it looks at what the store holds beside the bytes — the
verdict is user metadata, which every S3-compatible store answers with a
request per object. So the shape stays one shape and the tile stays one code
path, exactly as the paragraph above promises; what differs is whether this
response has anything to say about the check. Where the owner reads what
**stands** beside each of their photographs is the profile read's ``photos``
list (`ProfilePhotoResource`, ``docs/adr/0179`` §8) — the one screen whose
question is the check's answer, paying that request for at most three
objects rather than per tile.

**The upload can also carry nothing, and that is not the read's ``null``**
(``docs/adr/0138``). A reviewer that could not be asked concludes nothing, so
an outage answers ``null`` here rather than ``allowed``: fail-open used to
spell *nothing to warn about* with the only word it had, and that word now
means *checked and passed* somewhere else — on a player card, to somebody who
is not this photograph's owner. Both absences reach a client as *say
nothing*, which is what makes the collapse safe on this route and the
distinction load-bearing on the other one.

PhotoReviewDecision.title: PhotoReviewDecision
PhotoReviewDecision.description:
What the review port concluded about an image.

Two values, and there is deliberately no ``REJECTED``. The on-court check
**soft-warns rather than hard-blocks** (``docs/adr/0091``): a false reject
stops a real player on their first day, and that cost does not fall now that
the other side of the trade has got heavier. Adding a blocking value later is
an addition; shipping one now would be a behaviour nothing has earned.

There is also no value for *the reviewer could not be asked*, and there is
now a third state rather than two. This enum says what the reviewer
**concluded** about an image; *nobody looked* is not a conclusion about an
image, so it is spelled as the **absence** of one of these — ``None`` on a
verdict, no key on the object, no field on the wire (``docs/adr/0138``).
ADR-0133 already spelled the uploader's third state that way rather than
folding it into ``allowed`` at the boundary that knows least; the stored
verdict is the boundary that was folded, and this is where it is unfolded.
See `verdict_when_unreviewable` and `decision_on_record`.

PhotosResponse.title: PhotosResponse
PhotosResponse.description:
The photographs as the profile now holds them, in their order.

Ids and nothing else: the verdict beside each is the profile read's to
serve (`ProfilePhotoResource`), paid for once there rather than on every
rearrangement here.

PlayIntent.title: PlayIntent
PlayIntent.description:
What kind of game a player wants, in one sport.

Declared per ``(player, sport)`` — see ``play_intent_declaration.py`` for
why that is its own aggregate rather than a field on the profile.

PlayIntentDeclarationResponse.title: PlayIntentDeclarationResponse
PlayIntentDeclarationResponse.description:
The standing declaration for one player in one sport.

The **surface is not served back**. It is recorded beside the fact for us,
and a response that carried it would invite a client to render *where you
last said this*, which is a fact about the app and not about the player.

PlayIntentSurface.title: PlayIntentSurface
PlayIntentSurface.description:
Which screen a declaration was made on.

It is context recorded beside a fact, never a thing any decision branches
on.

**It is client-asserted and a client could lie about it** (ADR-0094). That
is accepted because the client is the only party that knows which screen it
was, and nothing load-bearing reads it — which is exactly the condition
under which a self-reported field is safe to keep.

**Three of its five screens are gone** — the search screen's toggle, the
deck and the drift prompt went with the searches (#579) — and their codes
stay, because a code already in a stream has to keep meaning what it meant
when it was written. Nothing emits them any more.

**It widened rather than renaming, and the reason was cost** (#280). The
deck earned the fifth member: ``POST /deck`` has no mode to read, so it
reads the declaration, is refused with ``play_intent_not_declared`` exactly
as a search is, and draws the same interstitial. Reporting that as
``SEARCH_SWITCH`` was a small untruth in the one field whose whole job is to
say which screen it was. The alternative argued was to rename
``SEARCH_SWITCH`` to ``PLAY_SWITCH`` — one value true of both Play surfaces
rather than two that each name one — and it lost on cost, not on taste: the
code is stored verbatim in ``PlayIntentDeclared`` and read back through
``PlayIntentSurface(event.surface)``, so a rename is an event migration
bought on a field nothing branches on, while a widening is one member and
leaves every code already in a stream meaning what it meant when it was
written.

PlayerProfileOptionsResponse.title: PlayerProfileOptionsResponse
PlayerProfileOptionsResponse.description:
Everything a client needs to *render* the profile steps, in one round trip.

A handful of facts rather than one endpoint each, because they are the same
kind of thing — closed, read-only, and needed by the same part of onboarding
at the same moment.

**Fields are only ever added.** A shipped mobile app parses this document for
months after it stops being built, so a new field goes on the end and the
ones already here keep their names and their types. ``search_radius`` is the
one removal, with the radius itself (#581), made while no build had shipped
anywhere but ``local``.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly Hours
weekly_hours.description: The hours of the week this player has ticked, in the platform's own reading order — day, then hour. **An empty list is a real answer** — a player may clear their week — and it means *we do not know when they play*, never *never*.

play_intents.title: Play Intents
play_intents.description:
What this player declared, per sport. **Only sports they have declared in appear** — an undeclared sport is absent and is never a `null` value, because there is no unanswered Play intent (`NO_PREFERENCE` is an explicit answer).

*Rated but not yet declared* is a set difference the client computes against `GET /ratings`, which it is already fetching to build the sport chips, and it is what lets a client open the one-tap interstitial for a sport still undeclared.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: The Social tag ids this player holds, **in the vocabulary's order** whatever order the picker sent them in. Required at commit, so never empty and never absent.

photos.title: Photos
photos.description: The photographs, **in the player's order** — the first is the profile photo — each with the verdict its uploader is owed. **An empty list is a real answer**: a profile may hold none, and the client draws the generated court poster.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description: The line this player wrote about themselves, as recorded, or **omitted** where none was written. Never an empty string (`docs/adr/0170`).

gender.description:
The owner's own answer to the gender question. **Served here and on no other response shape** (`docs/adr/0179` §4) — what one player is told about another never carries it.

**Omitted** on a profile committed before the question existed, and never read as `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`, which is an answer a player gives: a client pre-selects nothing rather than something.

gender_preference.description: Who the owner is willing to be matched with — their own setting, served here and on no other response shape (`docs/adr/0179` §4). Always present: it defaults to `ANY` at commit, so there is nothing for its absence to mean.

PlayerProfileReadResponse.title: PlayerProfileReadResponse
PlayerProfileReadResponse.description:
Every fact a player declared, in one round trip — what the Play screens
read and, since ``docs/adr/0179``, what the You tab draws its rows from.

**The gender and the preference are served here, and on no other shape.**
ADR-0096 §6's *no response shape carries a gender value out* is about
responses that describe one player to another, and its walk still refuses
both words on every one of those. A player reading their own answer on a
route scoped to ``me`` is not what that rule protects, and a screen that
asks *who should we match you with* with nothing pre-selected is a screen a
player cannot trust (``docs/adr/0179`` §4). ``gender`` is **omitted** on a
profile committed before the question existed — never ``PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY``,
which is an answer a player gives.

**The one thing still withheld is the location area**, and nothing stands
in for it: a profile cannot be committed without an area, so a
``has_location`` could never be false, and a branch nobody can take is a
branch nobody tests.

Absence has one spelling here and it is **omission** (``OMITTED``): an intro
never written, a photograph nobody looked at, a gender never asked. The one
absence that is served rather than omitted is **an empty ``photos`` list**,
because a profile may legally hold none and that is a real answer.

**No ``player_id``.** The resource is ``/players/me``, so the caller is the
bearer token and echoing it back would say nothing. ``GET /users/me`` is
where an id comes from.

**Fields are only ever added.** A shipped mobile app parses this document for
months after it stops being built. ``weekly_hours`` is the one replacement,
of the part-of-day ``availability`` it succeeded (``docs/adr/0189`` §5), and
``search_radius_km`` and ``proposals_opt_in`` the two removals (#581), each
made while no build had shipped anywhere but ``local``.

PlayerProfileResponse.title: PlayerProfileResponse
PlayerProfileResponse.description:
A player's profile as it now stands.

The same body whether the commit created the profile or replayed an earlier
one, so a client that only wants its profile needs no branch on the status.

**No gender value comes back out of this body**, and that is a rule rather
than an oversight (``docs/adr/0096`` §6): a preference crosses the wire
*in*, on a write; no response that describes one player to another carries
a gender out and no card renders one. This body is only ever the caller's
own profile, so nothing here would leak a third party's answer — the field
is left off anyway, because *which* shapes may carry it is a line rather
than a judgement made per endpoint, and the line is **exactly one shape**:
the owner's own read, ``PlayerProfileReadResponse`` (``docs/adr/0179`` §4).
The profile editor that reads it back is the You tab, and it reads that
route; the commit's answer stays what it was.

**Fields are only ever added.** A shipped mobile app parses this document for
months after it stops being built. ``weekly_hours`` is the one replacement,
of the part-of-day ``availability`` it succeeded (``docs/adr/0189`` §5), and
``search_radius_km`` and ``proposals_opt_in`` the two removals (#581), each
made while no build had shipped anywhere but ``local``.

is_self.title: Is Self
is_self.description:
Whether this is the reader's own record. **The server's answer, and the client never derives it** by comparing the id it asked about against its session — the sheet retitles to *How others see you* and drops the distance and the fit pill, and getting that wrong is most visible on the one screen it matters on. It decides the title and nothing on the sheet: every zone, what other players said included, is the same fact whoever is reading.

`true` on `/players/me/record` always, and on the parameterised route when a client asks about itself.

blocked_by_you.title: Blocked By You
blocked_by_you.description:
Whether **you** have blocked this person — your own block, and never theirs of you. Draw *Unblock* when `true` and *Block* when `false`, and no row at all when `is_self` is `true`.

**It answers one direction only, and that is the point.** Nothing on this response, or any other, says whether they blocked you: their record reads the same either way. If you both blocked, each of you reads `true` about your own block and nothing about the other's.

`false` on your own record, always. **Omitted only when your blocks could not be read** — draw neither row then, rather than a guess; the rest of the record is unaffected.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses the whole name or names nobody (``docs/adr/0171``). The title of the sheet.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: Their handle, drawn as `@nickname` under the name. **The record and the You tab are the only two places it is drawn** — never on a row, a card, a sentence, a sheet, a toast, a seat label or a spoken name — because two people may share a name and this is the screen a friend tells them apart on.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: The first photo — order is meaning in a photo list. **Omitted** when the player has no photograph, and the client draws the generated court poster rather than a placeholder.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description:
Short-lived signed URL that draws that photo. **Minted per response and stored nowhere** — this context stores nothing at all — so two reads of one record carry two links to one photograph.

**You cannot sign one yourself.** `GET /photos/{photo_id}` signs only *your own* photos and refuses a stranger's id deliberately, so this is the only address this photograph has.

**Present exactly when `photo_id` is.**

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about `photo_id`, or **omitted** where this photograph has not been checked.

**Omitted is not `allowed`, and only `allowed` earns a shield.** Three answers, not two: checked and passed, checked and flagged, and *nobody looked* — a photo that arrived while the reviewer could not be reached, or before the check existed at all. A client that drew a tick on the absence would be claiming a check happened on every photograph on the platform.

**A fact about this photograph and not about the player**, present only beside `photo_id`. `flagged` blocks nothing — the photo is stored, it is shown, and the check is wrong sometimes. The evidence behind the verdict never crosses on any route.

area_code.title: Area Code
area_code.description: Their coarse area, as a machine code. **An identifier and never a name** — nothing here can turn a coordinate into the name of a neighbourhood. What it licenses is the one comparison a client makes for itself: two players in the same square share a code, which is what *in your area* is drawn from.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: The Social tag ids they hold, in the vocabulary's own order. **Which of them the reader also holds is the client's own comparison** — the platform states no overlap here, so a record draws them untinted and claims nothing about common ground.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description:
One line this player wrote about themselves — their **intro** — verbatim, drawn under the name. **Omitted where they wrote none**, and never an empty string: the intro is optional, and a player who skipped has no line rather than an empty one.

Read off the profile as it stands. Fenced at the write against a phone number, an email, a URL or an `@handle`, so what arrives is a line about a player and never a way to reach one. Present on your own record as on anybody else's — it is what strangers read, shown back to you.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description:
One pill per sport they hold a rating in, **in the sport registry's own order** — the same order every list of sports on this surface takes, so a client never sorts one.

**Empty for somebody rated in nothing**, which is an ordinary state part way through onboarding rather than an error. It is empty exactly when `skill` is absent.

skill.description:
The skill card, for the one sport this sheet is about.

**Which sport is resolved here and stated back on the panel.** The `?sport=` you asked with wins where they are rated in it; otherwise it falls back to the sport they have played most, ties broken by the sport registry's own order. A fallback on their *highest* Level would make the header a boast about a sport nobody asked about.

**Omitted where no sport resolves** — that is, where they are rated in nothing at all. The header draws the poster with no Level on it, and there is no panel of noughts to mistake for a bad record.

reliability.description:
**What the platform watched them do** — the reliability pill and the metered rows it is the mean of.

**Omitted where nothing has ever fallen due for them**, which is most people today, and never a section of noughts: nobody has failed to turn up who was never due to. When it is omitted there is no `player_score` to draw a red pill from and no empty `strands` to head a card with.

**A third absence, asking a third question.** Not `skill`'s — somebody rated in four sports may have had nothing fall due at all. Not `variety`'s either, and they do not move together: a plan that dissolved and a seat that ran out are opportunities here and neither is a game anybody played.

It is about **no sport**, like `variety`: `?sport=` does not move it. Turning up is a habit, not a padel habit.

variety.description:
How widely they spread their games — **the raw pair, over their whole record.**

**Omitted where no counted game has ever been recorded for them**, which is not a nought and not `0 / 0`: a habit nobody has been observed having is not a narrow one. It is a **different absence from `skill`'s** — somebody rated in nothing may have played all week, and somebody rated in four sports may never have had a game counted.

**It is about every sport**, unlike `skill.last_five` above it. `?sport=` does not move it: a person who plays padel with the same four faces and squash with twenty has one habit, and a figure narrowed to one sport would be a different statistic under the same word.

sportsmanship.description:
**What other players said** — the average out of five and how many different people it rests on.

**Its own zone, deliberately apart from `reliability`.** That card promises *counted by the system, not written by people*, and this is the one thing here people wrote. Two headings, no lie.

**Omitted where nobody has rated them**, which is most people and is never a nought: rating is a favour, ignoring the card costs nothing, and nothing anywhere records that somebody did not answer. It is a **fourth absence** and asks a fourth question — not `skill`'s, not `variety`'s and not `reliability`'s, since a plan that dissolved and a seat that ran out are opportunities and neither is an opinion anybody offered.

**On your own record too, and it is the same figure.** What you read about yourself under *Sportsmanship, by players* is what a stranger reads about you — `4,3 / 5 · 12 players` — with nothing coarsened and no count withheld. The three-step band that used to stand in for it on your own sheet is gone from this shape; ADR-0179 §5 decides that and names what it costs.

**It is about no sport**, like `variety` and `reliability`: `?sport=` does not move it. How somebody is to play with is not a padel fact.

**The matcher never reads it.** A low figure hides nobody and demotes nobody — Pass and Block are the controls that act, and both are deliberate.

PlayerRecordResponse.title: PlayerRecordResponse
PlayerRecordResponse.description:
Everything the platform will say about one person, to this reader.

**Read through a prior disclosure and never about a person at large.** A
record opens for somebody you were on a game with, somebody you share a
group with, somebody in a group you run, and yourself. Anybody else — and
anybody a live gate no longer admits — is `404`, in one shape that names
nothing.

level_low.title: Level Low
level_low.description: The narrowed lower bound; `null` is the engine's own.

level_high.title: Level High
level_high.description: The narrowed upper bound; `null` is the engine's own.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start, as listed.

PostRequest.title: PostRequest
PostRequest.description:
*Post — you're In*: the four controls and the court hour picked on a
sheet. **Types only**: who it may be for and which court hours are offered
are the domain's to refuse, each with its own code.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What a seat costs if it fills.

challenger.description: Who posted it — `null` once they withdrew.

people_in.title: People In
people_in.description: Everybody In, in the order they said yes. No court number.

PostStillFillingSchema.title: PostStillFillingSchema
PostStillFillingSchema.description:
Somebody else's post still filling that the poster could join — **I'm
in** is `POST /proposals/{proposal_id}/yes`, free until it fills.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: How many versions it was dealt in, up to 3.

dealt_to.title: Dealt To
dealt_to.description: How many best fits were dealt it.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The seats open beside the poster.

PostedResponse.title: PostedResponse
PostedResponse.description: The post, In with its poster — its id is the game's, in *You're In*.

fits_free.title: Fits Free
fits_free.description: How many of the poster's best fits are free **together with them** at `best_starts_at` — the best hour in the range that has a free court, or with none, the best hour of the range — never people who overlap the poster at different hours. The client caps it at *5+*.

best_starts_at.title: Best Starts At
best_starts_at.description: The hour the number is read at; `null` with no hour ahead.

court_free.title: Court Free
court_free.description: A court the post could be made at is free in the range — the cell can be picked when somebody fits too.

full_game.title: Full Game
full_game.description: A full game's worth are free: `fits_free` reaches `open_seats`. Pickable with a court but not full is *only 2 fit · may not fill*.

outside_your_hours.title: Outside Your Hours
outside_your_hours.description: The poster's own week covers no hour the number could be read at: dimmed and dashed, still pickable.

happening.title: Happening
happening.description: The red dot: a rescue the poster is offered, or somebody else's post still filling they could join, starts in the range.

PostingCellSchema.title: PostingCellSchema
PostingCellSchema.description:
One day's range on the posting grid. **The client draws the nine looks
from these values** (the screens A5.2): *dead* is `fits_free` nought; *few*
or *enough* by `full_game`; a court glyph by `court_free`; *outside your
hours*, *past* and the red dot by their own flags. *Your pick* is the
client's.

day.title: Day
day.description: The day on the club's clock.

week.title: Week
week.description: `1` starts today; `2` is the seven days after.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant every cell was read against.

level_range.description: The range the others' Levels were counted in.

engine_level_range.description: The engine's own window for the kind around the poster's Level — the steppers' starting bounds, which may be narrowed in 0,05 steps and never widened.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The seats besides the poster: three in doubles, one in singles.

PostingGridResponse.title: PostingGridResponse
PostingGridResponse.description: **WHEN** — one week of the posting grid (the mechanics §9.1 step 5).

fits.title: Fits
fits.description: The best fits free at the cell's best hour, best fit first.

free_courts.title: Free Courts
free_courts.description: **Home club first**, then by hour. Tapping one picks it.

rescues.title: Rescues
rescues.description: **Already happening here**, first: booked games in the range with a seat offered to the poster — *I'm in · `share_grosze`* pays at once (`POST /bookings/{id}/seats`).

posts.title: Posts
posts.description: Then: posts still filling in the range the poster could join.

PostingSlotResponse.title: PostingSlotResponse
PostingSlotResponse.description: A cell's sheet (the mechanics §9.1 step 6; the screens A5.3).

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Whose *I was there* this confirms — somebody else's.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Permanent id — what a photos write carries

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about this photograph, or **omitted** where nobody looked.

**Omitted is not `allowed`.** Three answers, not two: checked and passed, checked and flagged, and *nobody looked* — a photo that arrived while the reviewer could not be reached, or before the check existed. This is the owner's own reading of the verdict the upload showed them once; `GET /photos/{id}` deliberately carries none. `flagged` blocks nothing — the photo is stored and shown, and the check is wrong sometimes. The evidence behind the verdict never crosses on any route.

ProfilePhotoResource.title: ProfilePhotoResource
ProfilePhotoResource.description:
One of the owner's photographs, and what the on-court check said about it.

**The same words as ``PhotoResponse``** — ``photo_id`` and ``review``, the
same code under the same name — so a client keys a tile from this list and
from ``GET /photos/{id}`` by one id and reads one vocabulary, even though the
two shapes spell *no verdict* differently (there ``null``, here omitted).
What differs is which route carries the verdict: the upload says it at
the moment the photograph was chosen (``docs/adr/0133``), the per-photo read
says nothing, and this list says what **stands** — because the You tab's
photos row is the one screen whose question is *what did the check conclude
about mine*, and a warning a player was shown once at upload has to be
findable again on the screen that lets them change the answer.

Three answers and only two values (``docs/adr/0138``): ``allowed``,
``flagged``, and **omitted** for *nobody looked*. Omitted is not
``allowed`` — a photograph that arrived while the reviewer was unreachable,
or before the check existed, has had nothing concluded about it, and a
client that drew a tick on the absence would be claiming a check happened.
``flagged`` blocks nothing: the photo is stored, it is shown, and the check
is wrong sometimes.

challenger.description: The poster of a challenge; `null` on a pick, and once its poster withdrew.

status.description: `FILLING` — seats are open: *Filling · `in_count` of `seats` in*. `WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT` — every seat is In and one player's refused share is awaited until `payment_due_by` (#625): their seat is theirs alone, and paying in time books it. `FILLED` — booked: `GET /bookings/{proposal_id}`. `EXPIRED`, `WITHDRAWN`, `COURT_HOUR_LOST` — it ended unfilled.

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: What the reader may do now, in the screen's order: `YES` and `NO` (*I'm in* / *Not this time*), `WITHDRAW` when they are In, `LEAVE` in its place while a payment is awaited — *Leave the game* with its sheet, sent as the withdrawal, `DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes` — and `CONFIRM_PAYMENT` when their seat waits on a refused payment (`your_payment`) — within their time to pay too, beside `LEAVE`; a payer refused for terms or a missing method has `YES` there, once fixed. Empty once the game is over or their answer is final.

your_payment.description: The payment to confirm to take the seat back — present exactly when `actions` holds `CONFIRM_PAYMENT`.

in_count.title: In Count
in_count.description: People In on the whole game.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: Four in padel and badminton, two otherwise.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

where.description: The club and its distance — never a court, given at booking.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: When the game leaves unfilled — *book by Sat 13:00*.

no_free_cancellation.title: No Free Cancellation
no_free_cancellation.description: The club's cut-off has already passed for this game.

indoor.title: Indoor
indoor.description: The kind of court the game promises — `true` *Indoor*, `false` *Outdoor* — when every free court it could be booked on is of that kind; `null` when they are mixed (Q122). Shown, never chosen by.

payment_due_by.title: Payment Due By
payment_due_by.description: When the payment the game waits for is due — *Waiting for one payment · until 14:40 · Nobody pays until it's in* (#625) — never whose. `null` unless `WAITING_FOR_A_PAYMENT`. The reader's own is `your_payment.confirm_by`.

time_to.description: What the time to `payment_due_by` is for (#638; Q113): `FIX_THE_CARD` — a hold refused before the club's cut-off, where nothing is taken; `PAY` — refused from it on. The others read *Waiting for one payment* either way; the payer's own words are `your_payment.time_to`'s. `null` with `payment_due_by`.

sides.description: Everybody drawn, the reader on their own side: for a reader still deciding, their own card as the deck deals it; for a reader In, everybody In — the client draws the open seats empty.

forecast.description: How even the game drawn is forecast — `null` where it cannot be read.

ProposalDetailsResponse.title: ProposalDetailsResponse
ProposalDetailsResponse.description:
A game still filling, as the reader opens it — the deck's card turned
into a screen.

ProposalStatus.title: ProposalStatus
ProposalStatus.description: Where a proposal stands for its details (the mechanics §14.2).

token.title: Token
token.description: The phone's Expo push token — `ExponentPushToken[…]` or `ExpoPushToken[…]` — as the notifications library hands it out.

QuestionResponse.title: QuestionResponse
QuestionResponse.description: A question in reading order: category, situation, question, answers.

RatingResponse.title: RatingResponse
RatingResponse.description:
One sport's Skill rating.

``mu`` and ``sigma`` are the Level and the Uncertainty — the same spelling
``ResultResponse`` already puts on the wire for the same two numbers, so a
client never has to learn that the rating it was just shown and the rating it
later reads back are described in two vocabularies.

RatingsResponse.title: RatingsResponse
RatingsResponse.description: Every sport this player is rated at — empty when they are rated at none.

ReadAs.title: ReadAs
ReadAs.description:
What the text was read as — so an empty answer can say which empty it is:
*no match for "…"* for text, *nothing at that link* for a link (#500
stories 37 and 38).

ReaderAction.title: ReaderAction
ReaderAction.description: What the reader may do from the details.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The payment. A share refunded has two rows under one id — the charge and the refund — told apart by `kind`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `CHARGE` — a share paid (✓, *−40 zł · paid*): taken at the club's cut-off, or at once after it; a share still held is no receipt (#637). `REFUND` — a share given back (↩, *+38,24 zł · refunded*): less exactly what was kept on the payment to a player who left after the cut-off when somebody took their seat, whole on a game its club cancelled after the cut-off. `RELEASED` — a share held for a booked game and let go untaken (*40 zł held · released*, #641): a leave before the cut-off, a game short at it, the club's cancel before it — so the hold the bank app showed is explained. Nothing was taken. A card checked when a game filled far ahead is never a receipt.

amount_grosze.title: Amount Grosze
amount_grosze.description: What was paid, what came back, or what was held, in grosze — always positive.

card_fee_grosze.title: Card Fee Grosze
card_fee_grosze.description: On a `REFUND`, exactly what was kept on the payment — *1,76 zł kept on your payment* — nought on a refund in full; never an estimate (#641). `null` on a `CHARGE` and a `RELEASED`.

paid_at.title: Paid At
paid_at.description: When the money moved: taken, or — on a `REFUND` — given back; on a `RELEASED`, when the hold was let go.

ReceiptSchema.title: ReceiptSchema
ReceiptSchema.description:
One share the reader paid, got back, or had held and let go — *the club
named as the seller*.

new_count.title: New Count
new_count.description: **The bell's number**: the notices that reached your list since you last opened it — given, or bundled into one and moving it up — never your own. Exact however many rows were asked for: the bell writes *99+* past 99. The same on every phone.

last_opened_at.title: Last Opened At
last_opened_at.description: When you last opened the list (`POST /players/me/notices/visit`), on any phone — `null` before the first time.

RecordLikelyRangeSchema.title: RecordLikelyRangeSchema
RecordLikelyRangeSchema.description:
The **likely range** a Level sits in — μ ± σ, clamped to the scale.

**Named for its surface, because the contract is one namespace and this
arrived second.** ``matchmaking`` already publishes a ``LikelyRangeSchema``
on the player card; a second class of that name does not shadow it, it
*renames* it — the emitted document qualifies both by module and every
generated type a shipped app already holds moves. It is ``games``' rule for
``GameStanding``, applied to the wire: the cost of a shared word is paid by
whoever arrives second.

The shape is deliberately identical to the card's. Two edges of one value,
both rounded by the engine, and a client computes neither.

average.title: Average
average.description:
The mean of what other players said, **out of five, to one decimal.** Served rather than derived: there is one mean and one rounding of this record on the platform, and it rounds halves up.

**One to five, and never nought.** There is no zero on the scale a player taps — a rating that reads as *worthless* is a weapon out of proportion to a tap — so a person nobody has rated is **absent** here rather than sitting at the bottom of it.

raters.title: Raters
raters.description:
How many **different people** the figure rests on. Always drawn beside it.

**People and not ratings.** Only a rater's most recent stars about somebody count, so ten evenings with the same partner contribute one. A high count is therefore evidence of breadth rather than of repetition, and it cannot be inflated by volume.

**At most fifty**, which is the window: the fifty most recent raters, each contributing the one answer that stands.

RecordSportsmanshipSchema.title: RecordSportsmanshipSchema
RecordSportsmanshipSchema.description:
What other players said — **the one thing here nobody counted.**

**Named for its surface, because the contract is one namespace.** The word
belongs to ``sportsmanship``, which has a surface of its own; a class simply
called ``SportsmanshipSchema`` here would not shadow whatever that context
publishes next, it would *rename both* — and every generated type a shipped
app already holds would move. It is ``RecordLikelyRangeSchema``'s rule.

**Its own heading, and never mixed with the rows above.** The record card is
headed *counted by the system, not written by people*, which is the promise
every metered row under it rests on; a number people typed sitting beneath
that title would make the title false. Draw this under *What opponents said*
and the two apart.

**Both numbers, always, from the very first rating.** There is no minimum
because the count does a minimum's work honestly: `4,7 / 5 · 17 players` and
`3,0 / 5 · 1 player` are the same field, and the second one visibly reads as
one person's opinion. Print them together — a figure drawn without its count
is this field's one way of lying.

**`raters` is people, not ratings.** Only somebody's most recent stars about
a person ever count, so a weekly partner is **one** rater however many
evenings they play. That is what makes a high count evidence of *breadth*.

**It is the fifty most recent raters and nothing is trimmed.** Somebody can
recover from a bad patch by playing with fifty other people; nobody's rating
is discarded for being an outlier, because deciding which raters were wrong
is a larger claim than publishing the number.

**The matcher does not read it, and you should say so if you draw it beside
the pill.** A low figure here does not hide anybody, demote anybody or keep
anybody out of a game — the reliability pill is the counted-only number and
is exactly what the platform acts on.

**On your own record too, at this resolution.** The person it is about
reads the same figure and the same count a stranger does; the coarse band
that used to stand in for it on their own sheet is gone from the shape. See
the field on the response for why.

player_score.title: Player Score
player_score.description:
Their **Player Score** out of a hundred — the same figure the player card prints and the reliability floor prices, at the same player-facing weights.

**It is the weighted mean of the `pct`s beneath it**, taken over the strands that are actually there: a name with nothing behind it costs nothing rather than dragging the number down. Read it rather than blending the rows yourself.

strands.title: Strands
strands.description:
The rows behind the figure, **in the strand vocabulary's own order** — never sort them.

**Only the strands this person has.** A strand nobody on this platform can measure and a strand nothing has fallen due under for *them* are the same absence here, and neither is a `0`: *we have not seen enough* and *they are bad at this* are different facts. There is always at least one row, because a panel with none is omitted whole.

ReliabilitySchema.title: ReliabilitySchema
ReliabilitySchema.description:
What the platform watched — the pill, and the rows it is the mean of.

**Counted by the system, not written by people.** Every row under this
heading is a ratio the platform observed. What opponents said about somebody
is not here and will not be: an opinion under this title would make the title
false.

**The pill is exactly the number the matcher acts on**, at the player's own
published weights. That is what makes the screen worth having — somebody who
works their record back up can watch the penalty lift — and it is why the
weights themselves are **not** on this response: they are a fact about how
the number is made, not about the person, and a client that had them could
print one strand as worth more than another, which no screen here claims.

ReliabilityStrand.title: ReliabilityStrand
ReliabilityStrand.description:
The six strands a reliability reading is built from, read separately.

The published Player Score blends them at 35/20/15/12/10/8 and the player
record prints each (``docs/adr/0140``). The two per-mode blends the ranking
weighed them by went with it (#580), so the published one is the only blend
left.

**The sixth name is not the one that was struck, and the difference is the
whole of ``docs/adr/0160``.** *Confirms results* asked whether a game reached
an agreed score, which is a fact about a **pair**, and every denominator
tried on it docked somebody ADR-0049 protects — both sides of an honest
disagreement included (``docs/adr/0137``). *Answers about results* asks
whether **this person** replied to a score put in front of them, and a
counter is as good an answer as an acceptance, so disagreeing costs nothing
and only silence is priced.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the seat leaves the board — the club's cut-off while it is ahead, then the start.

fills_by_the_cut_off.title: Fills By The Cut Off
fills_by_the_cut_off.description: *fills by Fri 16:00* — before the cut-off, the game is off unless its seats are taken by `deadline`; `false` is *offered until the start*. Switches by itself at the cut-off.

RescueOfferSchema.title: RescueOfferSchema
RescueOfferSchema.description: The open seat, offered to a reader not on the game (#545).

confidence_ceiling.title: Confidence Ceiling
confidence_ceiling.description: The highest `confidence` this engine version can reach, as a whole percent — a questionnaire has an irreducible limit, so a rating at this value was held by the ceiling and one below it by its own evidence. Absent only for a rating replayed from an engine version that has since been retired, which is the same case that carries no `confidence_reason`: such a rating keeps its numbers and loses its explanation. Do not hold a local copy of this number — it is version-scoped and may be retuned without a client release.

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: The card network as the provider names it, lower case — `visa`, `mastercard`, `unknown` for one it does not recognise. An open set: draw a plain card for a brand you have no badge for.

last_four.title: Last Four
last_four.description: The last four digits of the card number.

wallet.description: The phone's wallet it was saved through, or `null` for a card typed in.

admitted.title: Admitted
admitted.description: Everybody the switch to `ANYONE` admitted, **in the order they asked**. Empty for every other save.

SavedSettingsResponse.title: SavedSettingsResponse
SavedSettingsResponse.description: The group as its settings left it, and who the save let in.

ScoreSchema.title: ScoreSchema
ScoreSchema.description:
The sets, in the order they were played.

**A score names a winner**, and a level score is refused: none of the four
sports produces a draw, and *Last 5* is win or loss with no third column to
put one in. A *set* here is whatever the sport calls its unit — a set in
tennis and padel, a game in squash and badminton.

SearchMode.title: SearchMode
SearchMode.description:
What kind of game this is. **Two values, never three.**

``PlayIntent`` is a player's declaration and has three values; this is the
*game's* kind — a Games card is competitive or for fun — and has two. The
arities differ on purpose, so the likeliest bug in reading one as the other
is a type error rather than a paragraph in a document.

It picks the level window's tolerance (``matchmaking/domain/level_window.py``)
and nothing else here.

proposal_id.title: Proposal Id
proposal_id.description: The game it was for — a booking takes the same id.

status.description: `AUTHORISED` held, `FAILED` refused and waiting for its player, `HELD` held for the booked game until the club's cut-off and not paid (#637), `TAKING`/`CAPTURED` paid, `RELEASING`/`CANCELLED` let go untaken.

refusal.description: Why it was refused: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — confirm it in the app; `DECLINED` — confirm it with another card; `TERMS_NEEDED` — accept the terms again, then say yes; `NO_METHOD` — save a method, then say yes. `null` unless it was refused.

to_confirm.description: Present exactly while the payment waits for its player: confirm it with this, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

SeatChargeResponse.title: SeatChargeResponse
SeatChargeResponse.description: One of the reader's own seat charges.

SeatChargeStatus.title: SeatChargeStatus
SeatChargeStatus.description: Where a charge stands, as its stream leaves it.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` takes the seat — *I'm in · `share_grosze`* — and `GET /bookings/{id}` is its details as the reader sees it from outside.

kind.description: Competitive, or for fun (*· friendly* on the title).

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The dashed **?** squares after the players' posters.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the row leaves the board — the club's cut-off while it is ahead, then the start.

fills_by_the_cut_off.title: Fills By The Cut Off
fills_by_the_cut_off.description: *fills by `deadline`* before the cut-off; `false` is *offered until the start*. Switches by itself at the cut-off.

players.title: Players
players.description: Everybody on the game, each *paid* once the cut-off took their shares (#637) — the small posters, first side first. Long-press a poster for their record.

SeatToFillSchema.title: SeatToFillSchema
SeatToFillSchema.description:
One *Seats to fill* row: a booked game that lost a player, and the
reader fits and is free for it.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who holds this seat. ``null`` on a seat somebody has **left** and nobody has filled yet: the seat stays, drawn empty, and the game is awaiting a player before it can be recorded as played. **Always present** — a seat is never dropped.

name.title: Name
name.description:
The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses all of it or names nobody (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere.

``null`` where ``users`` no longer has this account, and on an open seat — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The seat stays: dropping it would publish a three-person doubles game, and the screen has a side to name instead.

SeatingSchema.title: SeatingSchema
SeatingSchema.description:
One position on one side: a person, or a seat somebody has left.

**The court is frozen until somebody leaves it** (``docs/adr/0162``). An
open seat is drawn, never dropped — `player_id` is `null` and the seat keeps
its place — so a four with one seat open is still a four and the client
folds *Needs a player* from it. Nothing on the wire names that rung.

**A name, and nothing else about them** (``docs/adr/0141``). A Level, a
band, an area and a run of form are what a *searcher* reads to decide about a
game that might happen, and a gate decided they may see them; this is the
record of a game that did, and it re-publishes nobody's profile off the back
of it. The court is the whole of the permission — ``GET /games`` answers
about games you were on the court of — so nothing here is re-gated against
who is reading.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

SellerSchema.title: SellerSchema
SellerSchema.description: The club a share is paid to — the seller, named on every receipt.

text.title: Text
text.description: What to say. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; empty after trimming is `message_is_empty`, and past the cap is `message_is_too_long`. **Neither is silently fixed** — a shortened message is one the sender believes they sent whole.

client_message_id.title: Client Message Id
client_message_id.description:
An id you generate for this send, **in the body rather than an `Idempotency-Key` header**, because it does two jobs: it makes a retry safe, and it is what you reconcile your optimistic bubble on.

**Send the same one on a retry.** A repeat answers `200` with the same message and the same `seq`, and records nothing — so a send that paused offline and resumed can never become two messages.

a.title: A
a.description: GameSide A's games in this set

b.title: B
b.description: GameSide B's games in this set

SetScoreSchema.title: SetScoreSchema
SetScoreSchema.description:
One set, **absolute**: what side A took, and what side B took.

Never relative to the reader. A score stored from one point of view has to be
flipped by whoever reads it next, and the first reader to forget publishes a
loss as a win.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly Hours
weekly_hours.description: Every hour still ticked. **The list is the week** — what is absent is unticked — and an empty list clears it, which is a legal value rather than a refusal.

SetWeeklyHoursRequest.title: SetWeeklyHoursRequest
SetWeeklyHoursRequest.description:
The weekly hours, replaced whole — *Save your week*.

**No floor, and that is the difference from the commit.** An empty list is a
cleared week and is recorded; ``weekly_hours_empty`` refuses the answer a
player is *asked for* at the end of onboarding, not every later edit of it.

Repeated hours are collapsed rather than refused, and the response carries
the week as it was stored — so a client that sent the same hour twice, or
sent the week in its own order, can see what the profile now holds.

ShareState.title: ShareState
ShareState.description:
Where the players' shares of a booked game stand (#637; the mechanics
§12.2, §14.1, Q113).

sport.description: Which sport this panel is about — **the resolved one, not the one asked for.** They differ whenever the subject holds no rating in the sport you arrived from.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level, as RacketSkill published it.

band.title: Band
band.description: The band's published name, as a key. The band's numeric edges are **not** here: they are not a second range to compare `likely_range` against.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description:
How sure the platform is, as a whole percentage — `rating`'s own figure and never re-derived here.

**It travels with `counted_games` and is meaningless without it.** A confident-looking number built on three games must not read like one built on forty, which is the whole reason both cross.

counted_games.title: Counted Games
counted_games.description:
**How many confirmed counted results have moved this Level, in this sport.** Deliberately not the player card's `counted_games`, which is how much they have *played*, over every sport, and includes an evening nobody agreed a score for.

This one is what the certainty rests on, so it comes off the same stream as the Level beside it and moves in step with it. **`0` is a real answer here** and is not an absence: a rating from the questionnaire that no game has tested yet is exactly what it says.

likely_range.description: The range their Level probably sits in, μ ± σ as the engine rounded it. Always present: two people both showing 2,75 are told apart by how wide this is.

last_five.title: Last Five
last_five.description:
Their last counted results **in this sport**, oldest to newest — the run of form drawn left to right.

**Per sport, which is the fix.** A run built across every sport and drawn beneath a single sport's Level was squash results under a padel number.

**Fewer than five is a real answer and is never padded**: three entries means three counted results, and the client draws the gap. An empty list means none of theirs has been counted and agreed.

**There are no dates here, at any granularity.** A moment beside one of these would be activity recency, which no surface on this platform carries in any shape.

SkillPanelSchema.title: SkillPanelSchema
SkillPanelSchema.description:
The skill card, for the one sport this sheet is about.

**The sport is resolved by the server and stated back.** You asked with
`?sport=`; what you get is that sport where they are rated in it, and
otherwise the one they have played most — so read `sport` here rather than
assuming the answer is what you sent.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole; `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the sport.

forecast.description: How even a game of the poster and them is forecast — `null` where it cannot be read.

SlotFitSchema.title: SlotFitSchema
SlotFitSchema.description: One of the poster's best fits free then — *2,75 · 93*.

SocialTag.title: SocialTag
SocialTag.description: The closed set of tag ids. An id here is permanent.

SocialTagGroup.title: SocialTagGroup
SocialTagGroup.description: The three groups, which are about the game and nothing else.

SocialTagGroupResource.title: SocialTagGroupResource
SocialTagGroupResource.description: One of the three groups, with its tags in the order they are rendered.

SocialTagResource.title: SocialTagResource
SocialTagResource.description:
One tag, as an id and nothing else — for now.

An object rather than a bare string deliberately: retiring a tag is
anticipated (an id is honoured forever and hidden from the picker), and a
tag that carries a field one day is an addition here, where an array of
strings would have to change element type — which breaks a shipped client.

minimum_tags.title: Minimum Tags
minimum_tags.description: Fewest tags a player may hold — the picker's floor

maximum_tags.title: Maximum Tags
maximum_tags.description: Most tags a player may hold — the picker's ceiling

SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource.title: SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource
SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource.description:
How many Social tags a selection must hold to be one.

The unit is in both field names: a bare ``minimum`` beside a list of
nineteen tags reads as a count of something, and which something is exactly
what a client would guess wrong.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: In the vocabulary's order, whatever order was sent.

SocialTagsResponse.title: SocialTagsResponse
SocialTagsResponse.description:
The tags as the profile now holds them — in the vocabulary's order.

A body rather than a ``204`` for the week's reason: the order stored is the
platform's and not the picker's, so a client that kept what it sent would
hold a selection in an order the profile does not.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description: The four sports Raketa rates, as a closed enum.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in it, as RacketSkill published it.

SportLevelSchema.title: SportLevelSchema
SportLevelSchema.description: One sport somebody is rated in, and their Level in it.
