sport.description: Which sport. The client draws its own dot and short form.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in it, as RacketSkill published it.

band.title: Band
band.description: The Level band's published name. **A key and never derived from the Level** — a client mapping a number to a band would be a second set of drawing constants, and the day the boundaries move the two would disagree.

SportPillSchema.title: SportPillSchema
SportPillSchema.description:
One sport this person is rated in, as a pill: the dot, the Level, the band.

**Narrower than the panel below it, deliberately.** A pill answers *what else
do they play*; how sure the platform is and what that rests on belong to the
one sport the sheet is about, and repeating them four times would be four
skill cards drawn as jewellery.

players.title: Players
players.description: Number of players the sport is played for

SportResource.title: SportResource
SportResource.description: One sport as served: how many play it and the durations it is sold in.

side.description: Which side put this score on the table

answer_by.title: Answer By
answer_by.description: When the other side's silence makes this score the result: 24 hours after it was put up, or after its last correction. **Nothing happens at this moment** — no job runs and nothing is written; the game simply reads as settled from here on. With two scores on the table, the later one's `answer_by` is when the game settles. *That's right* settles it at once, before this.

StandingProposalSchema.title: StandingProposalSchema
StandingProposalSchema.description:
One side's score, on the table and not yet settled on.

**At most one per side**, which is what bounds an argument to two rounds. Two
of them is a disagreement this platform does not arbitrate, and does not
hide: both scores travel, and either side may agree with the other's. If
neither does, the game settles when the later score's `answer_by` comes —
with the closer score if both name the same winner, and `DISPUTED` if they
name different winners.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: One of the other players on that court — in doubles an opponent or your partner, in singles the one opponent.

stars.title: Stars
stars.description: One to five whole stars. There is no zero and there are no halves.

StarsGivenSchema.title: StarsGivenSchema
StarsGivenSchema.description:
One player on the card, and the stars they were given.

``stars`` is declared as a plain integer **on purpose**. The range is one to
five whole stars and it lives in the domain, where a seed, a test and a
request all meet the same refusal; a Pydantic bound restating it here would
be a second copy of the rule, and the first of the two to be edited would win
silently for whichever callers went through it. A number off the scale comes
back as `stars_are_one_to_five`.

score.description: The score you say was played

StateResultRequest.title: StateResultRequest
StateResultRequest.description:
*This is the score.*

**One request for three acts**, and the record decides which: the first score
entered, a correction of your own side's while nobody has answered it, or
your side's disagreement with the other's. A client that named which would be
a client that could name it wrongly, and a mislabelled correction is a
proposal nobody may make.

**There is no rejection here and there is no body without a score.** An
objection carrying nothing would be free and always optimal for the loser.

strand.description:
Which strand this row is. **Key your copy off this code**, never off the row's position: a strand with nothing behind it is absent from the list entirely, so the rows you get are the rows this person has.

Three of the six names have no provider on this platform today and never appear here. They are listed on the enum because the vocabulary is closed and shared with the Fit breakdown, not because they are coming.

good.title: Good
good.description:
How many of those opportunities went the way the strand is named for — a game that was played, a booked game that was kept, a score that got a reply.

**A no is a good outcome on `ANSWERS_RESULTS`.** Countering a score you believe is wrong *is* answering it; what the strand prices is silence. **`KEEPS_PLANS` is broken only by leaving** a booked game so that it is called off at its cut-off, or after the cut-off with nobody taking the seat.

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.description:
How many times this fell due. **An opportunity and never a total**: a game still awaiting its entry, a booked game whose hour has not come and a score still inside its window are in neither half of this row, because publishing them either way would state a conclusion the clock has not reached.

**`ANSWERS_RESULTS` counts the last twelve months and the other rows count a career.** It is the one strand that forgets, so a player can work a bad month off it.

Never `0` — a row with nothing behind it is not drawn at all.

pct.title: Pct
pct.description:
The figure out of a hundred for this strand. **Served, never derived** — dividing `good` by `opportunities` yourself produces a fourth rounding of one record: this one rounds halves up, and the day a client rounds differently the two disagree by a point on exactly the values a player notices.

**Not the Fit breakdown's `StrandReading.value`**, which is the matcher's own reading of the same strand between 0 and 1. Two scales, two surfaces, two names — and `pct` is this contract's existing word for a whole percentage, as on the balance forecast.

StrandRowSchema.title: StrandRowSchema
StrandRowSchema.description:
One metered row: what fell due, what came of it, and the figure shown.

**All three cross, and the third is not a convenience.** `good` and
`opportunities` are the raw pair — a perfect record over nine and one over
forty are different claims, and a bar alone hides which. `pct` is the figure
the platform itself acts on, served so that a client is not the fourth place
this record gets rounded.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, as a machine code the client renders a sentence from. A booked game's room is told one: **`GAME_PLAYED`** — somebody said the game was played. **Draw nothing for a code you do not know**: the codes rooms opened by challenges carried are no longer written (#575).

**There is no *Game on* line.** The booked game is announced on Home and its details, and its room is born about it — a line saying so would be a second place for one fact to be true.

actor_id.title: Actor Id
actor_id.description: Who did it, or `null`. **Render `{name}` from the `people` on the response that carried this line** — the name is never repeated here, so a corrected one fixes the whole backlog. Not from `members` alone: whoever said they played may have left the court since, and `people` is where the read put their face.

values.title: Values
values.description: What the sentence needs beyond a name, and **nothing membership already says**. `GAME_PLAYED` carries nothing.

SystemLineSchema.title: SystemLineSchema
SystemLineSchema.description: What happened, as a code and its values. **Never a sentence.**

TimeTo.title: TimeTo
TimeTo.description:
What a refused share's thirty minutes are for (#638; the mechanics
§12.2, Q113) — one machinery, two names, decided by the club's cut-off.

TranscriptEntryResponse.title: TranscriptEntryResponse
TranscriptEntryResponse.description: One answered question: the question as it was asked, and what was chosen.

UncertaintyFactorResponse.title: UncertaintyFactorResponse
UncertaintyFactorResponse.description: Something that widened the range instead of moving the estimate.

UncountedReason.title: UncountedReason
UncountedReason.description: Why a game ended uncounted without anybody disagreeing about a score.

adult_attested.title: Adult Attested
adult_attested.description: The player's own claim that they are an adult. Required, and required to be `true`: the platform is adults only and that is a precondition of holding an account. `false` is refused with `adult_attestation_required`, and the client writes the sentence. **Not a date of birth and not age verification** — this records that the question was asked and answered, and nothing more.

UserCreateRequest.title: UserCreateRequest
UserCreateRequest.description:
Sign-up: credentials and the attestation, and nothing about who you are.

The nickname left this payload with ``docs/adr/0171`` §2 — it is asked in
onboarding, beside the name, with :class:`NameRequest`. **Extra fields are
refused** rather than ignored, so a client still sending one meets the
validation envelope instead of a sign-up that quietly dropped what it said.

name.title: Name
name.description: What this player is called — what every screen says. `null` until the naming — except on an account an invitation opened, which carries the name the club typed. The entry gate's first destination is **not named in full**: no name, or no nickname — and the naming step asks only for what is missing.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: The handle, unique across the platform, drawn as `@nickname` under the name on the You tab and nowhere else. `null` until the naming.

has_player_profile.title: Has Player Profile
has_player_profile.description: Whether this player has committed a Player profile — the fourth branch of the entry gate. Read from the profile's own event stream rather than from a projection, so it is correct immediately after the commit that creates one. False on a response that is not about the authenticated player, such as the one registration returns.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description:
The account, plus the one fact about it onboarding's entry gate needs.

``has_player_profile`` is not a property of a ``User`` and the domain layer
has no idea it exists — it is answered by the Player profile context and
joined here, on the response, because the gate reads it on every cold launch
and a second round trip for one boolean would be a second thing to fail
(``docs/adr/0090``).

``name`` and ``nickname`` are **null until the naming** — and each on its
own since ``docs/adr/0185`` §4, because an account an Invitation opened
carries the club-typed name and no nickname — and this is the one read
where either may be null (``docs/adr/0171`` §2): a player on any
surface that names another player has necessarily been named, because the
gate holds an unnamed account at the naming step. On ``/me`` they are read
from the player's own stream, as ``has_player_profile`` is, so they are
right the instant after the commit the gate reads them after.

**It is not an "onboarded" flag.** The rating context's invariant against one
stands: whether a player has been through onboarding *for a sport* is asked
by asking whether a rating exists for that sport, and this field cannot
answer it. This asks a genuinely per-player question, because a profile is
one per player and has no sport dimension at all.

Wallet.title: Wallet
Wallet.description:
The phone's own wallet a card was saved through. Only the two the setup
offers (the mechanics §12.4): Apple Pay on an iPhone, Google Pay on Android.
A card saved through any other wallet is recorded as a plain card.

day.title: Day
day.description: ISO weekday — 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. The grid is Monday-first.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: The hour the cell starts at, wall clock — 19 is 19:00 to 20:00. The week runs 07:00 to 23:00, so the first cell is 7 and the last is 22.

WeeklyHourResource.title: WeeklyHourResource
WeeklyHourResource.description:
One ticked hour of the week — a day, and the hour its cell starts at.

Two named fields rather than the single joined code the event stream stores.
The stream's code is a *storage* encoding chosen so a replay folds strings;
this is a contract a client renders a grid from, and a client that had to
split ``"3:19"`` would be parsing our persistence format.

**Every cell, and there is no exception.** The rule was twice read as
covering only the cells a player *chose* — the one a times rung offers
(#283), and the week a raised ``KEEP_THESE_TIMES`` quotes back (#286) — on
the argument that a payload handed back is not a resource. Both crossed as
codes, and in both cases a client ended up splitting one. What decides this
is not whose value it is but **what is done with it**: a cell that gets
drawn on the seven-by-sixteen grid crosses in these two fields, and the engine
holding it as a code is a fact about the engine. This side of the boundary
owns the encoding, so this side is where it is read.

WeeklyHoursResponse.title: WeeklyHoursResponse
WeeklyHoursResponse.description:
The weekly hours as the profile now holds them.

A body rather than a ``204`` because the value stored is not always the
value sent: repeated hours are collapsed and the order is the platform's
reading order, so a client that kept what it sent would hold a week the
profile does not.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: From the reader's Location area to the club, one decimal, never below a tenth — *3,1 km*. `null` for a reader with no Location area.

WhereSchema.title: WhereSchema
WhereSchema.description: WHERE: the club, and how far it is from the reader.

Who.title: Who
Who.description: Who a post is for (the mechanics §9.1 step 3).

Window.title: Window
Window.description:
When a game found on a week would plausibly be played. **A code, never a
sentence** — *"tonight"* is the client's word (``docs/adr/0022``).

**Derived, never chosen** (``docs/adr/0100``). There is no window picker
anywhere: a player changes their window by changing their week, which is the
same act that changes their matches. One control, one meaning.

It is a **label on the search**, not a proposed time — the week is still
never rendered to anybody as a calendar, and this says only how soon the week
it ran on comes round.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats nobody is In on yet, this player's yes counted. Nought on a game that booked, and on a full game waiting for one payment, whose seat is its payer's alone for their time to pay (#625).

booked.description: Present when this yes booked the game: every seat's share was held until the club's cut-off, or taken after it (#637), and the booking and its Game are open. `null` otherwise.

your_payment.description: Present when **this player's** share could not be held: nobody paid and the game did not book, and their time to pay runs to `confirm_by`. `null` otherwise — including when somebody else's could not (`payment_awaited_until`).

payment_awaited_until.title: Payment Awaited Until
payment_awaited_until.description: **This yes filled the game and a share was refused** (#625; Q110): the game waits for that payment until then — *It's a game!* with *Waiting for one payment · until 14:40 · Nobody pays until it's in*. Somebody else's, or this player's own (`your_payment`). `null` on every other answer — a rescue's refused payment too, whose seat is kept for its player alone and no game waits on it (`your_payment.confirm_by`, #640).

money.description: **The seat this answer took on a booked game** — a rescue's join, or its payment confirmed (#640; Q113): the joiner's money line, as Home reads it. `HELD` — *27 zł held until Fri 17:00*, taken at the club's cut-off (`free_to_leave_until`), and free to leave until then like everybody else; `CHECKED` — far ahead of the cut-off the card was only checked, and the share is held from `held_from`; `TAKEN` — after the cut-off, *you paid 27 zł* now. `null` on every other answer, and when the share was refused.

YesAnswerResponse.title: YesAnswerResponse
YesAnswerResponse.description:
What a yes left on the game — and, when it was the last, what the fill
did.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The refused payment: `GET /seat-charges/{id}` for what the phone confirms it with, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

refusal.description: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — the bank wants the player to confirm; `DECLINED` — confirm with another card; `TERMS_NEEDED` — accept the terms again, then say yes; `NO_METHOD` — save a method, then say yes.

confirm_by.title: Confirm By
confirm_by.description: **Their time to pay** (#625, #626; Q109) — before the club's cut-off, their time to fix the card (`time_to`, #638): the seat is theirs alone until then — *Confirm your payment by 14:40 to keep your seat*, or *Fix your card by 14:40* — every other hold kept, so paying in time books the game at once. Thirty minutes from the refusal, never past the book-by (nor, to fix, the cut-off). `null` once it ran out: the seat is open to others too, and still theirs to take back while it is free. **On a rescue** (#640) the seat is kept for them alone until then — *Fix your card by 14:40 to take the seat*, or after the cut-off *Confirm your payment by 14:40* — never past the game's start; `null` when none was kept, as for a rescuer whose kept seat ran out once already.

time_to.description: What the time to `confirm_by` is for (#638; Q113). `FIX_THE_CARD` — refused **before the club's cut-off**, where nothing is taken, only held: *Fix your card by 14:40 to keep your seat* — nothing is paid now, the same hold runs again once it is fixed, and the time never runs past the cut-off. `PAY` — refused from the cut-off on, where the money is taken at once: *Confirm your payment by 14:40*. `null` with `confirm_by`.

YourPaymentSchema.title: YourPaymentSchema
YourPaymentSchema.description:
This player's share could not be held when the game filled: nobody paid,
and their seat is open again until they confirm it or somebody takes it.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: The payment's secret. Confirm it in the provider's own fields.

connected_account_id.title: Connected Account Id
connected_account_id.description: The club's account at the provider — a direct charge is confirmed on the seller's account.

What the phone confirms a refused payment with, on the club's account:
the provider's own confirmation, with ``client_secret`` and the seller's
account — **asked of the provider now and never recorded**.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The payment to confirm: `GET /seat-charges/{id}` for what the phone confirms it with, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

refusal.description: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — the bank wants the player to confirm; `DECLINED` — confirm with another card.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: The latest moment the game can fill; past it the seat is gone.

confirm_by.title: Confirm By
confirm_by.description: **Their time to pay** (#625, #626; Q109) — before the club's cut-off, their time to fix the card (`time_to`, #638): the seat is theirs alone until then — *Confirm your payment by 14:40*, or *Fix your card by 14:40* — and the others' holds wait for it. `null` once it ran out: the row stays, without a time, while the seat is still free to take back.

time_to.description: What the time to `confirm_by` is for (#638; Q113): `FIX_THE_CARD` before the club's cut-off — *Fix your card by 14:40*, with a line that nothing is paid now; `PAY` after it — *Confirm your payment by 14:40*. `null` with `confirm_by`.
